definition_zh: 相互的；彼此的；共同的（后一义常被批评为宽松用法）
definition_en: given, felt, or done by each side toward the other in exchange; also shared in common by two or more parties
core_image: 两只手同时递出同一把钥匙：你给我，我也给你
scene: Two neighbours stand at the fence and hand each other a key to the other's gate; their help is mutual, since each one keeps a spare key for the other.
sceneCN: 这里 mutual 是「互相给予、彼此交换」（第 1 个义项：两方对等地给出并接受）；句意：两位邻居站在篱笆边，各自把对方院门的钥匙递给对方，他们的帮助是相互的，因为各自都为对方留了一把备用钥匙。图中可辨识物件：木篱笆、两把钥匙、两只同时伸出的手、两扇院门。

pos.zh: 相互的；彼此的；共同的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 互助主义者；互利共生的
使共有；把（企业）转为互助制

senses.title: Reciprocally given: both sides exchange
senses.titleCN: 互相给予：两边都在交换
senses.definition: given by each side to the other, so that what one gives is returned in kind
senses.definitionCN: 一方给出的，另一方也以同类回报；给予与接受同时发生在两边
senses.example: Their help was mutual: each repaired what the other had broken.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的帮助是相互的：各自修好了对方弄坏的东西。
senses.why: Late 15c. mutual was first used of feelings and meant 'reciprocally given and received'. The core picture is an exchange: I give, you give back.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪晚期 mutual 最先用于感情，义为“相互给予并接受”。核心画面是一次交换：我给，你也给回来。

senses.title: Mutual affection: a feeling each holds for the other
senses.titleCN: 相互的情感：各自对对方怀有同样的心
senses.definition: of a feeling, held by two people each toward the other, so that the regard is returned
senses.definitionCN: 指一种情感，两人各自对对方怀有，因而这份心意是被回应的
senses.example: The mutual affection between the two sisters lasted all their lives.
senses.exampleCN: 两姐妹之间的相互关爱持续了一生。
senses.why: A feeling can itself be the thing exchanged. Each heart holds the same regard, so the emotion is returned rather than held on one side only.
senses.whyCN: 情感本身就可以是被交换的东西。两颗心怀着同样的心意，因此这份情感是被回应的，而不是只停留在一边。

senses.title: The disputed mutual friend: a person known to both
senses.titleCN: 备受争议的 mutual friend：两人都认识的人
senses.definition: a person whom two other people both know, whether or not those two know each other through that person
senses.definitionCN: 两个人都认识的人，不论这两人是否正因此人而相识
senses.example: We met through a mutual friend at the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 我们经一位共同的朋友在博物馆相识。
senses.why: The 1630s 'common' sense let mutual describe what two parties share. Victorian critics attacked a mutual friend because a friend is not exchanged, yet the phrase is now standard.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 30 年代出现的“共同”义，让 mutual 可以形容两方共享之物。维多利亚时代的批评者攻击 a mutual friend，因为朋友并不是被“交换”的；但这一说法如今已属标准。

senses.title: Shared in common: a quality both possess
senses.titleCN: 共同拥有：两方都具有的性质
senses.definition: held or possessed in common by two or more parties, with no idea of exchange
senses.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同持有或拥有，不含交换之意
senses.example: Their mutual interest in birds began at the same observatory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对鸟类的共同兴趣始于同一座观测站。
senses.why: From the 1630s mutual widened from exchange to possession: two parties hold the same thing. This branch is the loose 'common' use that style guides still argue about.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 30 年代起，mutual 从“交换”扩展到“持有”：两方握着同一样东西。这条分支就是用法指南至今仍在争论的宽松“共同”义。

senses.title: Mutual benefit: advantage that runs both ways
senses.titleCN: 互利：双向流动的好处
senses.definition: producing advantage for each of the parties involved, so that neither gains at the other's expense
senses.definitionCN: 为涉及的每一方都带来好处，没有一方以另一方受损为代价获利
senses.example: The trade deal was based on mutual benefit rather than charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这项贸易协定建立在互利而非施舍之上。
senses.why: Benefit follows the exchange image: each side hands over something and receives something in return, so the gain travels in both directions.
senses.whyCN: benefit 延续了交换意象：每一方交出一些东西，又得到一些回报，因此好处是双向流动的。

senses.title: Mutual agreement: a promise binding both sides
senses.titleCN: 双方协议：约束两边的承诺
senses.definition: an arrangement accepted by both parties and binding each of them equally
senses.definitionCN: 两方都接受、并同等约束双方的安排
senses.example: They ended the lease by mutual agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们经双方同意终止了租约。
senses.why: An agreement is exchanged as promises: each gives a pledge and receives one. Because both are bound, the obligation is mutual in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 协议是以承诺作交换：各方给出一份保证，也收到一份保证。由于双方都受约束，这种义务是严格意义上的“相互的”。

senses.title: Mutual insurance: a company owned by its members
senses.titleCN: 互助保险：由会员共同拥有的公司
senses.definition: of an insurer or society owned by its policyholders, who share the risks and the profits
senses.definitionCN: 指由保单持有人共同拥有的保险机构，成员分担风险、共享收益
senses.example: The mutual insurance society returned part of the premium to every member.
senses.exampleCN: 这家互助保险社把部分保费返还给每位成员。
senses.why: Members pay in and cover one another, so the exchange is pooled rather than one-to-one. Mutual names the arrangement in which each member is both payer and owner.
senses.whyCN: 成员缴钱并相互保障，交换因此被汇聚起来，而不是一对一进行。mutual 命名的是这样一种安排：每个成员既是付款人又是所有者。

senses.title: Mutual fund: money pooled and shared
senses.titleCN: 共同基金：汇集并共享的资金
senses.definition: a fund in which many investors pool money and share the returns, recorded from 1950
senses.definitionCN: 众多投资者汇集资金并共享收益的基金，该说法记录于 1950 年
senses.example: She put her savings into a mutual fund rather than a single stock.
senses.exampleCN: 她把积蓄投入共同基金，而不是单只股票。
senses.why: Here mutual marks a pool: every investor holds a share of the same whole. The exchange is between members and the fund, and the ownership is shared.
senses.whyCN: 这里 mutual 标记的是一口“资金池”：每位投资者都持有同一整体的份额。交换发生在成员与基金之间，所有权则是共享的。

senses.title: Mutual relation: each term implies the other
senses.titleCN: 相互关系：每一项都蕴含另一项
senses.definition: in logic and mathematics, of a relation in which each of two terms entails or points to the other
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与数学中，指两项之间每一项都蕴含或指向另一项的关系
senses.example: In logic, entailment is mutual when each of two propositions follows from the other.
senses.exampleCN: 在逻辑中，当两个命题各自都能推出对方时，蕴含关系就是相互的。
senses.why: The exchange becomes formal: A gives support to B and B gives support back to A. Mutual relation names this perfect two-way dependency.
senses.whyCN: 交换在这里变得形式化：A 给 B 支撑，B 也给 A 支撑。mutual relation 命名的是这种完美的双向依赖。

senses.title: Mutual assured destruction: a guarantee aimed both ways
senses.titleCN: 相互确保摧毁：对准两边的保证
senses.definition: the Cold War doctrine that a full nuclear exchange would destroy both sides, so neither would strike first; abbreviated MAD in 1966
senses.definitionCN: 冷战理论：全面核交换将摧毁双方，因此谁都不敢先动手；1966 年缩写为 MAD
senses.example: Mutual assured destruction gave the Cold War its strangest acronym, MAD.
senses.exampleCN: 相互确保摧毁给冷战留下了最古怪的缩写 MAD。
senses.why: Each side guarantees the other's destruction, so the threat is returned in full. The word's exchange core hardens into a deadly symmetry.
senses.whyCN: 每一方都保证对方的毁灭，威胁被完整地回敬过去。这个词的“交换”核心在这里硬化成一种致命的对称。

intro.en: Mutual entered English in the late 15c. from Old French mutuel, and its first sense was an exchange of feeling, not joint ownership. The 'common' sense is a later and often criticised extension.
intro.cn: mutual 于 15 世纪晚期从古法语 mutuel 进入英语，最初的义项是情感的交换，而不是共同拥有。“共同”义是后来出现、且常受批评的扩展。

items.en: First recorded in the late 15c., used of feelings in the sense 'reciprocally given and received'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 15 世纪晚期，用于感情，义为“相互给予并接受”。

items.en: From Old French mutuel (14c.), which passed the Latin adjective into French.
items.cn: 来自古法语 mutuel（14 世纪），该词把拉丁语形容词带入了法语。

items.en: Latin mutuus meant 'reciprocal, done in exchange'; the stem mut- carries the idea of change and exchange.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus 意为“相互的、交换而成的”；词干 mut- 带有“改变、交换”的意思。

items.en: Traced to PIE *mei-(1) 'to change, go, move'. Watkins adds that its derivatives concern goods and services exchanged by custom or law.
items.cn: 可追溯至原始印欧语 *mei-(1)“改变、去、移动”。Watkins 补充说，该词根的衍生词与社会中按习俗或法律进行的货物与服务交换有关。

items.en: The sense 'common, shared' appears in the 1630s and was already noted as loosely misused, especially in a mutual friend.
items.cn: “共同的、共享的”义在 17 世纪 30 年代出现，当时就已被指出常被宽松误用，尤其见于 a mutual friend。

items.en: Mutual fund is recorded from 1950 and mutual assured destruction, or MAD, from 1966; both keep the two-way picture.
items.cn: mutual fund 记录于 1950 年，mutual assured destruction（缩写 MAD）记录于 1966 年；两者都保留了双向的画面。

note.en: The first group shares the mut- stem or sound, the second shares the meaning of two-way or shared, so form and sense stay apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享 mut- 词干或读音，第二组共享“双向／共享”的词义，这样词形与词义不会被混为一谈。

entries.definition: liable to change. It comes from Latin mutare 'to change', the same PIE family as mutuus, but means changeable rather than exchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 易变的。它来自拉丁语 mutare“改变”，与 mutuus 同属一个原始印欧语词族，但意思是“可变的”，不是“被交换的”。

entries.definition: a change of form or genetic material. It is built on mutare 'to change', not on mutuus 'reciprocal'.
entries.definitionCN: 形态改变；基因突变。它建立在 mutare“改变”上，而不是 mutuus“相互的”上。

entries.definition: to travel regularly to work, or to reduce a punishment. It comes from Latin commutare 'to exchange, change', com- plus mutare.
entries.definitionCN: 通勤；减刑。它来自拉丁语 commutare“交换、改变”，由 com- 加 mutare 构成。

entries.definition: given or done by each side to the other. It is the strict term for the exchange sense, while mutual also covers shared possession.
entries.definitionCN: 相互给予或做出的。它是“交换”义的严格说法，而 mutual 还覆盖“共同拥有”。

entries.definition: belonging to or shared by several. It states joint possession without any idea of giving and receiving.
entries.definitionCN: 共有的；共同使用的。它只说明共同拥有，不含给予与接受的意思。

entries.definition: done or shared by two or more parties acting together, as in a joint statement.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同做出或共享的，如 joint statement（联合声明）。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin stem mut-, the mutare family of mutable and mutation, and the documented history of mutual friend, mutual fund and MAD.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁词干 mut-、mutable 与 mutation 所属的 mutare 词族，以及 mutual friend、mutual fund、MAD 有据可查的历史。

normal.en: Picture an exchange: one hand gives a key, the other hand gives a key back. That is the original sense, 'reciprocally given and received'.
normal.cn: 想象一次交换：一只手递出钥匙，另一只手也递回钥匙。这就是本义“相互给予并接受”。

normal.en: Mutable, mutation and commute all carry Latin mutare 'to change'; mutual carries the same stem for an exchange of things or feelings.
normal.cn: mutable、mutation、commute 都带拉丁语 mutare“改变”；mutual 用同一词干表示物品或情感的交换。

normal.en: A mutual friend is a person both parties know, which is why critics call the phrase a loose use of 'common'.
normal.cn: a mutual friend 是两方都认识的人，正因如此，批评者说这个短语是对 common 的宽松误用。

normal.en: A mutual fund pools money, and mutual insurance pools risk: both are modern institutions built on shared ownership.
normal.cn: mutual fund 汇集资金，mutual insurance 汇集风险：两者都是建立在共同所有权上的现代制度。

normal.en: The standard frames are mutual respect, mutual understanding, mutual benefit and mutual agreement.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是 mutual respect、mutual understanding、mutual benefit 与 mutual agreement。

abstract.en: Two arrows drawn head to head: each direction needs the other, and a single arrow would not be mutual.
abstract.cn: 画两支箭头对着彼此：每个方向都需要另一边，只画一支就不叫 mutual。

abstract.en: A two-pan balance with equal weights: nothing tips, because what is given on one side is returned on the other.
abstract.cn: 一架两盘天平，两边砝码相等：哪边都不下沉，因为一边给出的在另一边被回敬。

abstract.en: Take one partner away and the word loses its point: mutual always needs a second party in the picture.
abstract.cn: 拿走一方，这个词就失去意义：mutual 的画面里永远需要一个“另一方”。

examples.en: The two countries signed the treaty out of mutual interest, not friendship.
examples.cn: 两国签署这项条约是出于共同利益，而非友谊。

examples.en: Mutual respect kept the debate civil even when the disagreement was sharp.
examples.cn: 相互尊重让这场辩论即使分歧尖锐也保持文明。

examples.en: They were introduced by a mutual friend who knew both families.
examples.cn: 他们是由一位认识两家人的共同朋友引见的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谬球」——两人把同一个球互相抛来抛去，你抛给我、我抛给你 → mutual 相互的、彼此的

root: 源自拉丁语 mutuus“相互的、交换而成的”，可追溯至原始印欧语 *mei-(1)“改变、移动”，核心是双方交换，而非共同拥有。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of mutual all grow from one picture: two parties handing something to each other. From exchanged feeling it extends to shared possession, then to contracts, member-owned institutions, formal relations and finally to the deadly symmetry of MAD.
sensesIntro.cn: mutual 的十个义项都从同一幅画生长出来：两方把东西递给对方。从被交换的情感，它扩展到共同拥有，再扩展到契约、会员共有的机构、形式关系，最后到 MAD 那种致命的对称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands passing the same key to each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一把钥匙互相递过去。

branches.en: THE EXCHANGE CORE: reciprocal action and reciprocal feeling, the oldest and strictest sense.
branches.cn: 交换核心：相互的行为与相互的情感，最古老也最严格的义项。

branches.en: SHARED, NOT EXCHANGED: the disputed mutual friend and the wider 'common' sense.
branches.cn: 共享而非交换：备受争议的 mutual friend，以及更宽的“共同”义。

branches.en: BENEFIT AND CONTRACT: advantage that runs both ways, and promises that bind both sides.
branches.cn: 利益与契约：双向流动的好处，以及约束双方的承诺。

branches.en: POOLED OWNERSHIP: member-owned insurance and the mutual fund, where sharing becomes an institution.
branches.cn: 汇聚式所有权：会员共有的保险与共同基金，共享在此变成制度。

branches.en: FORMAL SYMMETRY: mutual entailment in logic and the mutual destruction of the nuclear standoff.
branches.cn: 形式对称：逻辑中的相互蕴含，以及核对峙中的相互摧毁。

intro.en: Mutual is Latin mutuus plus the adjective suffix -al. English then builds mutually, mutuality, mutualism, mutualist, mutualize and mutualization, while the bare stem mut- lives on in mutation, mutable and commute.
intro.cn: mutual 是拉丁语 mutuus 加形容词后缀 -al。英语随后构造出 mutually、mutuality、mutualism、mutualist、mutualize 与 mutualization，而光秃的词干 mut- 仍活在 mutation、mutable、commute 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutuus 'reciprocal, done in exchange' is the direct source; the same stem gives mutare 'to change' and commutare 'to exchange'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus“相互的、交换而成的”是直接来源；同一词干还给出 mutare“改变”与 commutare“交换”。

items.meaning: reciprocal; shared by two sides
items.meaningCN: 相互的；双方共享的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The agreement rests on mutual trust.
items.exampleCN: 这项协议建立在相互信任之上。

items.meaning: in a reciprocal way, each toward the other
items.meaningCN: 相互地；彼此地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two plans are mutually exclusive.
items.exampleCN: 这两个方案互相排斥。

items.meaning: the quality of being reciprocal
items.meaningCN: 相互性；共同性（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The contract depends on the mutuality of the promises.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同依赖于承诺的相互性。

items.meaning: a system of mutual dependence, or a symbiotic partnership
items.meaningCN: 互助主义；互利共生（-ism 构成体系名词）
items.example: Certain ants and plants live in mutualism.
items.exampleCN: 某些蚂蚁与植物处于互利共生关系。

items.meaning: a supporter of mutualism, or an organism in a mutual partnership
items.meaningCN: 互助主义者；互利共生的一方（-ist 构成人或形容词）
items.example: The coral and its algae are mutualists.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚与它的藻类是互利共生的一方。

items.meaning: to convert an enterprise into member ownership
items.meaningCN: 使共有；转为互助制（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The society voted to mutualize the savings bank.
items.exampleCN: 该协会投票决定把储蓄银行转为互助制。

items.meaning: the process of becoming member-owned
items.meaningCN: 共有化；互助化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Mutualization changed how the insurer was governed.
items.exampleCN: 互助化改变了这家保险公司的治理方式。

items.meaning: a change of form or genetic material
items.meaningCN: 变化；基因突变（mut-“改变”+ -ation）
items.example: The mutation gave the moths a darker wing.
items.exampleCN: 这次突变让蛾子的翅膀变深了。

items.meaning: capable of being changed
items.meaningCN: 易变的；可改变的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: Language is mutable, and slang changes fastest.
items.exampleCN: 语言是可变的，而俚语变化最快。

items.meaning: to travel regularly, or to exchange one penalty for another
items.meaningCN: 通勤；减刑（com-“共同、交换”+ mut-“改变”）
items.example: She commutes by train every morning.
items.exampleCN: 她每天早上乘火车通勤。

definition_en: to state that something is not true, to make something ineffective, or to deny a proposition
core_image: 在整句话上盖一枚红色“否”字章，把整行划掉
scene: A lawyer stamps VOID across a clause to negate it, while the clerk crosses out the whole line.
sceneCN: 这里 negate 是「使无效、取消」（第 4 个义项：用正式手段使条款或行为失效）；句意：律师在一项条款上盖下“作废”章，使它失效，书记员把整行划掉。图中可辨识物件：合同纸、红色“作废”章、被划掉的条款、书记员的笔。

pos.zh: 否认；否定；使无效；取消

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

derivatives.zh: 否定的；负面的；负片；负数

senses.title: Deny a statement: say it is not true
senses.titleCN: 否认一句话：说它不成立
senses.definition: to state that a claim or statement is false
senses.definitionCN: 声明某项主张或说法是假的
senses.example: The witness negated every claim in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 证人否认了报告中的每一项主张。
senses.why: The Latin verb negare meant 'deny, say no'. Negating a statement is simply placing a no against it, so the word begins as a spoken refusal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 negare 意为“否认、说不”。否定一句话，就是在这句话前面放一个“不”，因此这个词最初是一个说出口的拒绝。

senses.title: Deny the value or existence of an idea
senses.titleCN: 否定一个观念的价值或存在
senses.definition: to reject the truth, value, or reality of an idea rather than of a single sentence
senses.definitionCN: 否定一个观念的真实性、价值或存在，而不是否定某一句话
senses.example: Nothing in the new evidence negates the value of the old method.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据中没有任何东西能否定旧方法的价值。
senses.why: The same 'say no' moves from a sentence to a whole idea. What is denied is no longer a wording but the standing of a belief.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“说不”从一句话移到整个观念。被否认的不再是措辞，而是一种信念的地位。

senses.title: Cancel out an effect: make an advantage useless
senses.titleCN: 抵消效果：让优势失去作用
senses.definition: to make the effect of something ineffective, so that its benefit disappears
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物的作用失效，使其好处消失
senses.example: Heavy rain negated the advantage of our early start.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨抵消了我们提早出发的优势。
senses.why: From 'say no to a claim' the word extends to 'say no to an effect': the advantage is treated as cancelled, as if a line were struck through it.
senses.whyCN: 从“对主张说不”扩展到“对效果说不”：优势被当作已被注销，就像上面划了一道线。

senses.title: Void a clause or a formal act
senses.titleCN: 使条款或正式行为作废
senses.definition: to cancel the legal force of a clause, order, or formal act
senses.definitionCN: 取消条款、命令或正式行为的法律效力
senses.example: The court negated the clause that barred workers from suing.
senses.exampleCN: 法院使那条禁止工人起诉的条款失效。
senses.why: A legal act exists by being valid. Saying no to its validity makes it nothing, so negate here means to render null and void.
senses.whyCN: 法律行为靠“有效”而存在。对它的有效性说不，就使它归零，因此这里的 negate 意为“使失效、作废”。

senses.title: Logical negation: deny a proposition
senses.titleCN: 逻辑否定：否定一个命题
senses.definition: in logic, to form the proposition that is true exactly when the original is false
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑中，构造一个当原命题为假时恰好为真的命题
senses.example: To negate 'all swans are white' is to assert that at least one swan is not white.
senses.exampleCN: 否定“所有天鹅都是白的”，就是断言至少有一只天鹅不是白的。
senses.why: Logic turns the spoken no into an operator. Negation does not merely disagree; it reverses the truth value of the whole proposition.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把口头的“不”变成一个运算符。否定不只是不同意，而是把整个命题的真值翻转过来。

senses.title: Grammatical negation: mark a clause with not
senses.titleCN: 语法否定：用 not 一类词标记小句
senses.definition: in grammar, to make a clause negative with words such as not, never, no, or nothing
senses.definitionCN: 在语法中，用 not、never、no、nothing 等词使小句变为否定
senses.example: Adverbs such as 'never' negate the clause they appear in.
senses.exampleCN: never 这类副词会使其所在的小句变为否定。
senses.why: The same neg- morpheme appears in not and no. Grammar gives the refusal a fixed slot, so negate names the mechanical process of marking a clause negative.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 neg- 词素也出现在 not 与 no 中。语法为拒绝提供了一个固定位置，因此 negate 也指把小句标成否定的机械过程。

senses.title: Rebut a motion in debate
senses.titleCN: 辩论中驳倒一项动议
senses.definition: in formal debating, to oppose and argue against a motion so that it is defeated
senses.definitionCN: 在正式辩论中反对并论证击败一项动议
senses.example: The second speaker negated the motion with three independent arguments.
senses.exampleCN: 第二位辩手用三个独立论点驳倒了这项动议。
senses.why: A motion is a proposal put forward for acceptance. To negate it is to say no to the proposal as a whole, which in debate means arguing the other side.
senses.whyCN: 动议是提出来等待通过的提案。否定它，就是对整个提案说不；在辩论中，这就是站到另一边论证。

senses.title: Neutralize a military capability
senses.titleCN: 使军事能力失效
senses.definition: to make an enemy capability or weapon ineffective, so that it no longer counts
senses.definitionCN: 使敌方能力或武器失效，使其不再构成作用
senses.example: The new battery negated the enemy's artillery range.
senses.exampleCN: 新的炮台使敌方火炮的射程优势失效。
senses.why: In warfare an advantage is cancelled as a claim is cancelled: the capability is still there, but its effect is struck out.
senses.whyCN: 在战争中，优势像主张一样被注销：能力还在，但它的作用被划掉了。

senses.title: Flip the sign of a number
senses.titleCN: 把数的符号翻转
senses.definition: in mathematics and computing, to reverse the sign of a value, turning positive into negative or the reverse
senses.definitionCN: 在数学与计算中，反转一个值的符号，把正变负或把负变正
senses.example: The program negates the value before storing it.
senses.exampleCN: 程序在存储该值之前先把它取负。
senses.why: If a number has a direction, negating it sends it the opposite way. The 'no' becomes a mirror: the same magnitude, the opposite sign.
senses.whyCN: 如果数带有方向，取负就把它送向相反方向。“不”在这里变成一面镜子：大小相同，符号相反。

senses.title: Cancel a result: wipe out a score or outcome
senses.titleCN: 取消结果：抹掉得分或成果
senses.definition: to cancel an achieved result, such as a goal or a gain, so that it no longer stands
senses.definitionCN: 取消已经取得的结果，如进球或收益，使其不再成立
senses.example: A foul in the final second negated the winning goal.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一秒的犯规使那粒制胜球失效。
senses.why: A result stands only if it counts. Negating it removes it from the record, which is the same 'strike it out' gesture applied to an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 结果只有在“算数”时才成立。否定它，就是把它从记录中划掉，这是同一个“划掉”动作用在成果上。

intro.en: Negate is built on Latin negare 'deny, say no', whose neg- is the same negative element as PIE *ne- 'not'. English gained the verb late, by back-formation from negation or directly from the Latin participle negatus.
intro.cn: negate 建立在拉丁语 negare“否认、说不”之上，其中的 neg- 与原始印欧语 *ne-“不”是同一个否定成分。英语较晚才得到这个动词，途径是从 negation 逆构，或直接取自拉丁语过去分词 negatus。

items.en: Latin negare 'to deny, say no', with past participle negatus and the noun negatio, is the source of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 negare“否认、说不”，及其过去分词 negatus 和名词 negatio，是整个词族的来源。

items.en: Negare goes back to PIE *ne- 'not', the same element behind English no and not; neg- is thus a negative morpheme, not a root meaning 'thing'.
items.cn: negare 可追溯至原始印欧语 *ne-“不”，英语的 no 与 not 也出自同一成分；因此 neg- 是否定词素，而不是表示“物”的词根。

items.en: Negation is recorded in the 15c., arriving through Old French negacion and Latin negationem, both from negare.
items.cn: negation 记录于 15 世纪，经古法语 negacion 与拉丁语 negationem 传入，二者都出自 negare。

items.en: A few isolated uses of the verb negate appear in the 1620s, but they did not establish the word.
items.cn: 动词 negate 在 17 世纪 20 年代有个别用例，但并未使这个词立足。

items.en: The verb is established in 1795, either back-formed from negation or taken directly from the Latin participle negatus.
items.cn: 该动词于 1795 年确立，或由 negation 逆构而来，或直接取自拉丁语过去分词 negatus。

items.en: The neg- family remains visible in negative, deny, abnegate, renegade and negligible, all built on the same 'say no' element.
items.cn: neg- 词族仍可见于 negative、deny、abnegate、renegade、negligible，它们都建立在这个“说不”的成分上。

note.en: The first group shares neg- or a similar shape, sometimes with a different sense of the same element; the second group shares the idea of denying or cancelling.
note.cn: 第一组共享 neg- 或相近词形，其中有的虽是同一成分却另有一义；第二组共享“否认或取消”的意思。

entries.definition: to discuss in order to reach an agreement. It comes from Latin negotium 'business', literally nec otium 'not leisure', so its neg- means 'not' but points to work rather than denial.
entries.definitionCN: 谈判；协商。它来自拉丁语 negotium“事务”，字面是 nec otium“并非闲暇”，所以它的 neg- 虽也表示“不”，指向的却是工作而非否认。

entries.definition: too small to matter. It comes from neglegere 'to neglect', literally 'not to pick up', with neg- 'not' plus legere 'to pick'.
entries.definitionCN: 微不足道的。它来自 neglegere“忽视”，字面是“不去拾起”，由 neg-“不”加 legere“拾取”构成。

entries.definition: expressing denial, or below zero. It is the adjective from negare, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 否定的；负的。它是 negare 的形容词形式，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: to state that something is not true or that one does not possess it. It is the everyday verb, while negate often sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 否认某事为真，或声称自己不具有某物。它是日常动词，而 negate 常显得正式。

entries.definition: to make a law, contract, or result legally invalid. It stresses the legal effect that negate can also carry.
entries.definitionCN: 使法律、合同或结果在法律上无效。它强调 negate 也能携带的那层法律效力。

entries.definition: to prove a statement or argument wrong by evidence. It goes further than negate, which may only deny.
entries.definitionCN: 用证据证明某说法或论点错误。它比 negate 更进一步，因为 negate 可以只是否认。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: neg- is the negative element shared with no and not, and the family includes negation, negative, deny, abnegate and renegade.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：neg- 是与 no、not 共享的否定成分，词族包括 negation、negative、deny、abnegate、renegade。

normal.en: neg- is the same negative piece as in no and not: negate is literally 'to no' a statement.
normal.cn: neg- 与 no、not 中的否定成分相同：negate 字面上就是对一个说法“说不”。

normal.en: negation, negative and negator are the noun, adjective and agent built on the same stem.
normal.cn: negation、negative、negator 是同一词干上的名词、形容词与施动者。

normal.en: deny, abnegate and renegade all keep negare 'to deny': to deny a claim, to deny oneself, and to deny one's faith.
normal.cn: deny、abnegate、renegade 都保留 negare“否认”：否认主张、否定自我、否认信仰。

normal.en: In logic a negation reverses truth value; in grammar not, never and no do the same work in a clause.
normal.cn: 逻辑中否定翻转真值；语法中 not、never、no 在小句里做同样的工作。

normal.en: The legal picture is a stamp marked VOID: the clause still exists on paper, but its force has been struck out.
normal.cn: 法律画面是一枚“作废”章：条款仍在纸上，但它的效力已被划掉。

abstract.en: A red no stamped across a whole page: not one word is corrected, the entire page is refused.
abstract.cn: 整页纸上盖一个红色“不”：一个字都没改，整页都被拒绝。

abstract.en: Two mirror-image numbers, plus three and minus three: negation keeps the size and flips the direction.
abstract.cn: 两个镜像数字，正三与负三：否定保留大小，只翻转方向。

abstract.en: A door marked NO ENTRY still has a handle: the thing exists, but its use has been negated.
abstract.cn: 一扇写着“禁止入内”的门仍有把手：东西还在，但它的用途已被否定。

examples.en: The new evidence negated the claim that the lake was safe for swimming.
examples.cn: 新证据否定了这个湖可以安全游泳的说法。

examples.en: One late goal negated everything the visiting team had built in the first half.
examples.cn: 一粒迟来的进球抹掉了客队在上半场建立的一切。

examples.en: In formal logic, you negate a proposition by asserting that it is false.
examples.cn: 在形式逻辑中，你通过断言一个命题为假来否定它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「你盖特」——你盖的章一律被划掉、被说“不算” → negate 否定、使无效

root: 源自拉丁语 negare“否认、说不”，来自原始印欧语 *ne-“不”；neg- 是否定词素，与英语 no、not 同源，不是表示实物的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of negate all come from one gesture: putting a no against something. The no can fall on a statement, an idea, an effect, a clause, a proposition, a clause in grammar, a motion, a weapon, a number, or a result.
sensesIntro.cn: negate 的十个义项都来自同一个动作：对某样东西说“不”。这个“不”可以落在陈述、观念、效果、条款、命题、语法小句、动议、武器、数字或结果上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red no stamped across a line until it no longer counts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个红色“不”盖在一行字上，直到它不再算数。

branches.en: SPOKEN DENIAL: refusing a statement, then refusing a whole idea.
branches.cn: 口头否认：先拒绝一句话，再拒绝整个观念。

branches.en: STRIKING OUT: cancelling an effect, and wiping out a result that had already been achieved.
branches.cn: 划掉：抵消一种效果，以及抹掉已经取得的结果。

branches.en: FORMAL CANCELLATION: voiding a clause in law, and defeating a motion in debate.
branches.cn: 正式取消：在法律上使条款作废，在辩论中驳倒动议。

branches.en: LOGIC AND GRAMMAR: reversing a proposition's truth value, and marking a clause with not.
branches.cn: 逻辑与语法：翻转命题的真值，以及用 not 标记小句。

branches.en: TURNING TO THE OPPOSITE: neutralizing a capability, and flipping the sign of a number.
branches.cn: 转向反面：使能力失效，以及翻转数字的符号。

intro.en: Negate is neg- 'no' plus the verb ending -ate. English builds negation, negative, negatively, negator and abnegation on the same stem, while deny, renegade, negligible and negotiate carry the same negative element in other shapes.
intro.cn: negate 是 neg-“不”加动词词尾 -ate。英语在同一词干上构造出 negation、negative、negatively、negator、abnegation；而 deny、renegade、negligible、negotiate 以别的形态携带同一个否定成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin negare 'to deny, say no' and its participle negatus are the direct source; negatio and negativus supply the noun and adjective patterns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 negare“否认、说不”及其分词 negatus 是直接来源；negatio 与 negativus 提供了名词与形容词的模式。

items.meaning: to deny, cancel, or make ineffective
items.meaningCN: 否认；取消；使无效（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The new rule negates the old exemption.
items.exampleCN: 新规定使旧的豁免失效。

items.meaning: the act or result of denying; a negative statement
items.meaningCN: 否定；否定句（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The negation of a true statement is false.
items.exampleCN: 真陈述的否定是假的。

items.meaning: expressing denial, or below zero
items.meaningCN: 否定的；负面的；负的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The test gave a negative result.
items.exampleCN: 检测结果呈阴性。

items.meaning: in a denying or harmful way
items.meaningCN: 否定地；负面地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The delay affected the project negatively.
items.exampleCN: 延误对项目产生了负面影响。

items.meaning: a word or person that negates
items.meaningCN: 否定词；否定者（-or 构成施动名词）
items.example: In English, 'not' is the commonest negator.
items.exampleCN: 在英语中，not 是最常见的否定词。

items.meaning: to renounce or deny oneself something
items.meaningCN: 放弃；克制（ab-“离开”+ neg-“否认”，即把欲望否认掉）
items.example: The monk abnegated all personal possessions.
items.exampleCN: 这位修士放弃了所有个人财物。

items.meaning: a person who deserts a cause or faith
items.meaningCN: 叛教者；变节者（字面是“再次否认”自己的信仰）
items.example: The party called him a renegade for joining the rival camp.
items.exampleCN: 该党称他为变节者，因为他加入了对手阵营。

items.meaning: to state that something is not true
items.meaningCN: 否认；拒绝给予（de- 加强 + neg-“说不”）
items.example: She denied ever seeing the letter.
items.exampleCN: 她否认曾见过那封信。

items.meaning: too small or unimportant to consider
items.meaningCN: 微不足道的（字面是“不值得拾起”，neg-“不”+ leg-“拾取”）
items.example: The difference in cost was negligible.
items.exampleCN: 成本上的差别微不足道。

items.meaning: to discuss in order to reach an agreement
items.meaningCN: 谈判；协商（neg-“不”+ otium“闲暇”，即“不是闲事”的事务）
items.example: The two sides negotiated for six hours.
items.exampleCN: 双方谈判了六个小时。

latinEntries.meaning: denied, having been said no to

definition_zh: 网络；网状系统；人脉；广播网；联网
definition_en: an interconnected system of lines, people, or devices, or to connect things into such a system
core_image: 一张撒开的渔网：每个网结都连着别的网结
scene: A fishing net lies spread across the deck, and its knots form a network that links every part to the next.
sceneCN: 这里 network 是「网状结构、网络」（第 1 个义项：由线或节点交织成的网）；句意：一张渔网摊在甲板上，网结连成一张网，把每一处都连到下一处。图中可辨识物件：渔网、网结、甲板、缆绳、渔船。

pos.zh: 网络；网状系统；人脉网；广播网
用网覆盖；联网；建立人脉

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

derivatives.zh: 联网；建立人脉；网络化（network 的动名词）
网；罗网；用网捕（network 的第一成分）

senses.title: A mesh of connected lines: netting
senses.titleCN: 连成一片的网线：网状织物
senses.definition: a structure of cords or threads crossed and knotted so that every part is linked to the rest
senses.definitionCN: 由绳线交叉打结而成的结构，每一处都与其他部分相连
senses.example: A torn network of netting lay across the harbour stones.
senses.exampleCN: 一张破了的网摊在港口的石头上。
senses.why: Network began in the 1550s as net plus work, literally a net-like fabric or structure. The picture is physical: knots joined by threads.
senses.whyCN: network 在 16 世纪 50 年代由 net 加 work 构成，字面是“网一样的织物或结构”。画面是实体的：网结被网线连起来。

senses.title: An interlocking transport system
senses.titleCN: 交织的交通系统
senses.definition: a system of rivers, canals, roads, or railways that cross and connect at many points
senses.definitionCN: 河流、运河、道路或铁路在许多点上交叉相连的系统
senses.example: A network of canals linked the inland farms to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 一张运河网把内陆农场与港口连了起来。
senses.why: The 1839 sense 'any complex, interlocking system' was first used of rivers, canals and railways. The mesh becomes a map of routes.
senses.whyCN: 1839 年出现的“任何复杂交织的系统”一义，最初用于河流、运河与铁路。实体的网变成了一张路线图。

senses.title: A broadcasting system of many transmitters
senses.titleCN: 由多个发射台组成的广播网
senses.definition: a group of radio or television stations that share programmes and transmit them over a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 共享节目、向广大地区播送的广播电台或电视台群体
senses.example: The radio network broadcast the speech to forty stations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家广播网把演讲播送到四十家电台。
senses.why: From 1914 the word named a broadcasting system of multiple transmitters. Signals travel from node to node, so the mesh becomes a web of stations.
senses.whyCN: 从 1914 年起，这个词指由多个发射台组成的广播系统。信号从一个节点传到另一个节点，网于是变成了一张电台之网。

senses.title: An interconnected group of people
senses.titleCN: 彼此相连的人群
senses.definition: a group of people who are connected through work, family, or shared interests and can help one another
senses.definitionCN: 通过工作、家庭或共同兴趣相连、能互相帮助的一群人
senses.example: Her network of former classmates helped her find work.
senses.exampleCN: 她由老同学组成的人脉网帮她找到了工作。
senses.why: The 1934 sense came from psychology: people as nodes, relationships as threads. The mesh is now social rather than physical.
senses.whyCN: 1934 年的义项来自心理学术语：人是节点，关系是网线。此时网是社会性的，而非实体的。

senses.title: A computer network: machines that talk
senses.titleCN: 计算机网络：会互相通信的机器
senses.definition: a set of computers and devices connected so that they can exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 为交换数据而连接起来的一组计算机与设备
senses.example: The lab's computers share one network and one printer.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室的计算机共用一个网络和一台打印机。
senses.why: When computers became nodes, the old mesh needed no new shape: each machine is a knot, each cable a thread. The word kept its picture and changed its material.
senses.whyCN: 当计算机成为节点时，这张网不需要新形状：每台机器是一个结，每根线缆是一根网线。词保留了画面，只换了材料。

senses.title: A utility grid: power and telephone lines
senses.titleCN: 公用事业网：电力与电话线路
senses.definition: the connected system of cables, pipes, or lines that carries power, water, or telephone signals
senses.definitionCN: 输送电力、水或电话信号的互联电缆、管道或线路系统
senses.example: The power network failed during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间电网瘫痪了。
senses.why: A grid is a mesh laid over a region. Power lines join substations as knots join threads, so network names any utility system with that shape.
senses.whyCN: 电网是铺在一片区域上的网。电线把变电站连起来，正如网线把网结连起来，因此 network 可指任何具此形状的公用系统。

senses.title: To cover with a net
senses.titleCN: 用网罩住
senses.definition: to cover an area or object with netting, usually for protection
senses.definitionCN: 用网覆盖一片区域或一个物体，通常是为了保护
senses.example: They networked the orchard to keep the birds off the fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用网罩住果园，防止鸟啄食果实。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1887 with the plainest sense: to put a net over something. It turns the noun's object into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义于 1887 年出现，意思最直白：把网盖在某物上。它把名词所指的对象变成了一个动作。

senses.title: To broadcast across a network
senses.titleCN: 通过广播网播送
senses.definition: to send a programme out through several linked stations at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时通过多家相连的电台或电视台播送节目
senses.example: The show was networked across the whole country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节目通过广播网在全国播送。
senses.why: From 1940 the verb meant to distribute a programme through a network of transmitters. The broadcast travels along every thread of the mesh.
senses.whyCN: 从 1940 年起，动词指通过发射台网络分发节目。广播沿着这张网的每一根线传出去。

senses.title: To connect computers together
senses.titleCN: 把计算机连成网
senses.definition: to link computers or devices so that they can share data
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机或设备连接起来，使它们能共享数据
senses.example: Engineers networked the two sites with fibre-optic cable.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用光纤把两个站点联网。
senses.why: The 1972 computing sense turns the noun into a task: you tie new knots into the existing mesh until the machines can reach one another.
senses.whyCN: 1972 年的计算机义把名词变成一个任务：你把新的结系进已有的网里，直到机器能彼此抵达。

senses.title: To build professional contacts
senses.titleCN: 建立职业人脉
senses.definition: to meet and cultivate useful contacts, especially for work
senses.definitionCN: 结识并经营有用的人脉，尤指为工作目的
senses.example: She networks at every conference she attends.
senses.exampleCN: 她每参加一次会议就经营一次人脉。
senses.why: The 1982 sense applies the verb to people: each new acquaintance is a knot added to a personal mesh. Nothing physical remains but the shape.
senses.whyCN: 1982 年的义项把动词用在人身上：每位新认识的人都是加入个人之网的一个结。实体消失了，只剩形状。

intro.en: Network is a plain English compound of net and work, first recorded in the 1550s for net-like fabric. Its modern senses are a series of metaphors laid on that mesh: transport in 1839, broadcasting in 1914, people in 1934, and finally computers.
intro.cn: network 是 net 与 work 的朴素英语复合词，16 世纪 50 年代首次记录，指网一样的织物。它的现代义项是一层层叠加在这张网上的比喻：1839 年的交通、1914 年的广播、1934 年的人群，最后是计算机。

items.en: Net is Old English net 'net, snare', a word old enough to serve as a metaphor for a moral or mental trap.
items.cn: net 是古英语 net“网、罗网”，这个词古老到可以被用作道德或心理陷阱的比喻。

items.en: Network is first recorded in the 1550s as net plus work, meaning a net-like fabric or structure.
items.cn: network 于 16 世纪 50 年代首次记录，由 net 加 work 构成，指网一样的织物或结构。

items.en: The sense 'any complex, interlocking system' appears in 1839, first applied to networks of rivers, canals and railways.
items.cn: “任何复杂交织的系统”一义出现于 1839 年，最初用于河流、运河与铁路的网络。

items.en: A network becomes a broadcasting system of multiple transmitters in 1914.
items.cn: 1914 年，network 开始指由多个发射台组成的广播系统。

items.en: The sense 'interconnected group of people' appears in 1934 as psychological jargon.
items.cn: “彼此相连的人群”一义于 1934 年出现，原为心理学术语。

items.en: The verb follows: to cover with a net in 1887, to broadcast in 1940, to link computers in 1972, and to build contacts in 1982.
items.cn: 动词随后跟进：1887 年“用网覆盖”，1940 年“通过广播网播送”，1972 年“计算机联网”，1982 年“建立人脉”。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, including a phrase that sounds like network; the second group is chosen for the mesh image they share.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写与读音挑选，其中有一个听起来像 network 的短语；第二组按它们共享的网状意象挑选。

entries.definition: the total value of assets minus liabilities. The phrase sounds almost like network but belongs to finance, not to nets.
entries.definitionCN: 资产总值减去负债。这个短语听起来几乎和 network 一样，但属于财务，与网无关。

entries.definition: a small, low-cost laptop of the late 2000s. It joins net to book, not to work.
entries.definitionCN: 21 世纪末流行的小型低价笔记本电脑。它把 net 与 book 组合，而不是与 work 组合。

entries.definition: material made of net or mesh. It is the noun from net, not a form of network.
entries.definitionCN: 网材；网。它是 net 派生的名词，不是 network 的变形。

entries.definition: a mesh spun by a spider, or any complex system of linked parts. It stresses threads woven by a maker, while network stresses nodes joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 蜘蛛结的网，或任何由相连部分构成的复杂系统。它强调由造物者织出的线，而 network 强调节点之间的连接。

entries.definition: a pattern of crossing lines, especially for power or streets. It is regular and geometric, while a network can grow irregularly.
entries.definitionCN: 交叉线构成的格网，尤指电网或街道网。它是规则、几何的，而 network 可以不规则地生长。

entries.definition: a material of connected strands with open spaces between them. It names the fabric itself rather than the system it forms.
entries.definitionCN: 由相连线股构成、中间有空隙的材料。它指织物本身，而不是织物形成的系统。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: net plus work in 1550s, then the dated extensions to transport, broadcasting, people and computers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：16 世纪 50 年代的 net 加 work，随后是有年代可查的扩展——交通、广播、人群与计算机。

normal.en: net plus work says the whole thing plainly: work made of net, a net-like fabric.
normal.cn: net 加 work 说得很直白：用网做成的制成品，即网一样的织物。

normal.en: In 1839 the mesh became a map: rivers, canals and railways crossing at many points.
normal.cn: 1839 年，这张网变成了一张地图：河流、运河与铁路在许多点上交叉。

normal.en: In 1914 the mesh became stations: many transmitters sharing one broadcast.
normal.cn: 1914 年，这张网变成了电台：多个发射台共享一次广播。

normal.en: In 1934 people became the nodes, and in 1972 computers did: the shape stayed, the material changed.
normal.cn: 1934 年人成了节点，1972 年计算机成了节点：形状没变，材料变了。

normal.en: The verbs follow the nouns: cover with a net, broadcast, connect, and build contacts.
normal.cn: 动词跟随名词：用网覆盖、播送、联网、建立人脉。

abstract.en: Picture one knot with four threads leaving it: remove the threads and it is only a knot; the connections are what make it a network.
abstract.cn: 想象一个网结向四面伸出四根线：抽掉线，它只是个结；正是连接使它成为网络。

abstract.en: The same drawing works for a map, a radio system, a group of friends, and a room of servers.
abstract.cn: 同一幅图可以画成地图、广播系统、朋友圈，也可以画成一屋子的服务器。

abstract.en: Cut one thread and the mesh still holds: a network is judged by how many routes remain, not by any single knot.
abstract.cn: 剪断一根线，网仍然撑得住：网络的价值在于还剩多少条通路，而不在任何一个结。

examples.en: A dense network of trails connects the villages along the valley.
examples.cn: 一张密集的小路网连接着山谷里的村庄。

examples.en: The company rebuilt its computer network after the outage.
examples.cn: 停电事故后，公司重建了计算机网络。

examples.en: He spent the conference networking with editors and researchers.
examples.cn: 他在会议上忙着与编辑和研究人员建立人脉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内特网」——内里特别多网结，四面八方都连着 → network 网络、人脉

root: 由古英语 net“网、罗网”加 work“工作、制成品”复合而成，1550s 首次记录，核心是“网一样的连结结构”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of network all keep one shape: knots joined by threads. The material changes from cord to canals, transmitters, people, cables and computers, and the verb senses simply put the mesh into action.
sensesIntro.cn: network 的十个义项都保留同一个形状：网结被网线连起来。材料从绳索换成运河、发射台、人、电缆与计算机，动词义只是让这张网动起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fishing net spread out, every knot tied to others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张摊开的渔网，每个网结都连着别的结。

branches.en: FROM FABRIC TO MAP: literal netting, then a system of rivers, canals and railways.
branches.cn: 从织物到地图：字面的网，然后是河流、运河与铁路构成的系统。

branches.en: FROM STATIONS TO PEOPLE: transmitters sharing programmes, then people sharing contacts.
branches.cn: 从电台到人：共享节目的发射台，然后是共享关系的人。

branches.en: TECHNICAL GRIDS: computers exchanging data, and utility lines carrying power or signals.
branches.cn: 技术性网络：交换数据的计算机，以及输送电力或信号的公用线路。

branches.en: THE OLD VERBS: covering with netting, and sending a programme through many stations.
branches.cn: 较早的动词：用网覆盖，以及通过多家电台播送节目。

branches.en: THE MODERN VERBS: linking machines, and cultivating a personal web of contacts.
branches.cn: 现代动词：连接机器，以及经营个人的关系网。

intro.en: Network is the compound net plus work, with no Latin suffix. English adds -ing, -ed, -er and -able to it, and the same net appears in internet, intranet, netting and netbook.
intro.cn: network 是 net 加 work 的复合词，不含拉丁后缀。英语在它上面加 -ing、-ed、-er、-able，而同一个 net 也出现在 internet、intranet、netting、netbook 中。

latinIntro.en: Network is Germanic, not Latin. The Latin entries below are its nearest counterparts, given for contrast: rete 'net', nexus 'a binding', and nectere 'to bind'.
latinIntro.cn: network 属日耳曼语，不属拉丁语。下面列出的拉丁词是它最接近的对应词，仅供对照：rete“网”、nexus“联结”、nectere“捆缚”。

items.meaning: a mesh-like structure or connected system
items.meaningCN: 网状结构；相连的系统（net“网”+ work“制成品”）
items.example: The city's tram network covers the whole centre.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市的有轨电车网络覆盖了整个市中心。

items.meaning: the act of linking systems or building contacts
items.meaningCN: 联网；建立人脉（-ing 构成动名词）
items.example: Networking is half of the value of a conference.
items.exampleCN: 建立人脉是一场会议一半的价值。

items.meaning: connected into a network
items.meaningCN: 联网的；连成网的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The whole campus is networked.
items.exampleCN: 整个校园都已联网。

items.meaning: a person skilled at building contacts
items.meaningCN: 善于建立人脉的人（-er 构成人称名词）
items.example: She is the best networker in the sales team.
items.exampleCN: 她是销售团队里最会经营人脉的人。

items.meaning: a mesh of cord used to catch things
items.meaningCN: 网；罗网（network 的第一成分）
items.example: The fishermen repaired the net before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 渔民在黎明前修补了渔网。

items.meaning: mesh material
items.meaningCN: 网材；网（-ing 构成材料名词）
items.example: Netting protected the young trees from deer.
items.exampleCN: 网罩保护了小树不被鹿啃食。

items.meaning: the worldwide network of computers
items.meaningCN: 互联网（inter-“在……之间”+ net“网络”）
items.example: The files were sent over the internet.
items.exampleCN: 文件通过互联网发送。

items.meaning: a private network inside an organisation
items.meaningCN: 内联网（intra-“在内部”+ net“网络”）
items.example: Staff read the policy on the company intranet.
items.exampleCN: 员工在公司内联网上读到这项政策。

items.meaning: a small laptop designed mainly for online use
items.meaningCN: 上网本（net“网络”+ book，指主要用于上网的小电脑）
items.example: He carried a netbook instead of a full laptop.
items.exampleCN: 他带了一台上网本，而不是完整的笔记本电脑。

items.meaning: capable of being connected to a network
items.meaningCN: 可联网的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: The printer is networkable and shared by the office.
items.exampleCN: 这台打印机可联网，供全办公室共用。

latinEntries.meaning: a net, a network of cords

latinEntries.meaningCN: 联结；联系（来自 nectere“捆缚”）

definition_zh: 中立的；中性的；不带电的；空挡的；中性色的
definition_en: not taking either side in a conflict, neither acid nor alkaline, carrying no charge, or being neither one nor the other of two
core_image: 拔河绳上的红布停在两条界线正中间：两边都不到
scene: A referee stands between two wrestlers with both arms down and stays neutral, favouring neither.
sceneCN: 这里 neutral 是「不选边、不介入」（第 2 个义项：在两方冲突中不偏向任何一方）；句意：裁判站在两名摔跤手之间，双臂下垂，保持中立，不偏向任何一方。图中可辨识物件：摔跤垫、两名选手、居中站立的裁判、下垂的双臂。

pos.zh: 中立的；中性的；不带电的；空挡的
中立者；中立国；（机械）空挡

collocations.zh: 中立的语气；平淡的语气

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 中立主义者；中立主义的
中子（不带电的粒子，名字即来自 neutral）

senses.title: Alchemical balance: opposing elements in proportion
senses.titleCN: 炼金术的平衡：对立元素按比例相抵
senses.definition: in alchemy, of a substance made from opposing elements that balance each other exactly
senses.definitionCN: 在炼金术中，指由相互对立的元素按比例恰好相抵而成的物质
senses.example: Alchemists called a body neutral when fire and water balanced in it.
senses.exampleCN: 当火与水在物体中相抵平衡时，炼金术士称该物体为 neutral。
senses.why: Neutral is first recorded in the 1540s in alchemy, where opposite qualities were thought to cancel each other. The core picture is a scale that stops exactly in the middle.
senses.whyCN: neutral 最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，用于炼金术，当时认为对立的性质会相互抵消。核心画面是一架恰好停在正中的天平。

senses.title: Not taking sides: outside a conflict
senses.titleCN: 不选边：置身冲突之外
senses.definition: not supporting either party in a dispute, war, or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在争端、战争或争论中不支持任何一方
senses.example: The referee stayed neutral and let both sides speak.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判保持中立，让双方都把话说完了。
senses.why: The alchemical balance became a social one: two opposing sides cancel, and the person in the middle belongs to neither. This sense is recorded alongside the first.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术的平衡变成了社会的平衡：两个对立面相互抵消，中间的人不属于任何一边。这个义项与最早义项同时被记录。

senses.title: Chemistry: neither acid nor alkaline
senses.titleCN: 化学：非酸非碱
senses.definition: of a solution, having a pH near seven, neither acidic nor basic
senses.definitionCN: 指溶液 pH 接近七，既非酸性也非碱性
senses.example: Pure water is neutral, with a pH close to seven.
senses.exampleCN: 纯水是中性的，pH 接近七。
senses.why: Chemistry took the balance image literally: acid and alkali cancel, and the middle point is neutral. The sense is recorded from the 1660s.
senses.whyCN: 化学把这个平衡意象落到实处：酸与碱相抵，中间点就是中性。该义项记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。

senses.title: Not a belligerent: outside the war
senses.titleCN: 非交战国：站在战争之外
senses.definition: of a country or ship, not belonging to either side in a war
senses.definitionCN: 指国家或船只不属于战争中的任何一方
senses.example: Neutral shipping was allowed through the blockade.
senses.exampleCN: 中立国的船只被允许通过封锁线。
senses.why: A state can hold the same position as the referee: it takes no side, so its ships and ports stay outside the fighting. The sense is recorded from 1711.
senses.whyCN: 国家可以处在和裁判相同的位置：不选边，因此它的船只与港口留在战斗之外。该义项记录于 1711 年。

senses.title: Colour: low saturation, easy to live with
senses.titleCN: 颜色：低彩度、耐看
senses.definition: of a colour, muted and close to grey or beige, used as a quiet base
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色柔和、接近灰或米色，用作安静的底色
senses.example: The room was painted in neutral greys and warm beiges.
senses.exampleCN: 房间刷成了中性灰和暖米色。
senses.why: A muted colour sits between the strong hues and commits to none. The balance image moves from substances to light, and the sense is recorded from 1821.
senses.whyCN: 柔和的颜色处在各种强烈色相之间，不偏向任何一种。平衡意象从物质移到光线，该义项记录于 1821 年。

senses.title: Electrical neutrality: no net charge
senses.titleCN: 电中性：净电荷为零
senses.definition: having equal positive and negative charge, so that no net charge remains
senses.definitionCN: 正负电荷相等，因此没有净电荷残留
senses.example: A neutron carries no charge and is electrically neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 中子不带电荷，是电中性的。
senses.why: Positive and negative charges cancel exactly as acid and alkali cancel. The word's balance is now counted in charge rather than in qualities.
senses.whyCN: 正负电荷的相抵，正如酸与碱的相抵。这个词的平衡现在以电荷计算，而不是以性质计算。

senses.title: A neutral party: the person or state in the middle
senses.titleCN: 中立的一方：处在中间的人或国家
senses.definition: a person, country, or place that takes no side, often chosen to host talks
senses.definitionCN: 不选边的人、国家或地点，常被选作会谈地点
senses.example: The talks were held in a neutral, far from both capitals.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈在一个远离两国首都的中立地点举行。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the party that holds the middle position. Recorded as a noun in the mid-15c., it names whoever the balance leaves uncommitted.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指占据中间位置的一方。该名词义在 15 世纪中期已有记录，命名的是被天平留在“未承诺”状态的那一方。

senses.title: Mechanical neutral: no gear engaged
senses.titleCN: 机械空挡：没有齿轮咬合
senses.definition: of a gearbox, in the position where no gear is engaged and no power reaches the wheels
senses.definitionCN: 指变速器处在没有齿轮咬合、动力不传到车轮的位置
senses.example: He shifted into neutral and let the car roll to a stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他挂入空挡，让车滑行到停下。
senses.why: In a gearbox the middle position transmits nothing: neither forward nor reverse. The sense, recorded from 1905, is the balance image in metal.
senses.whyCN: 在变速器里，中间位置什么也不传递：既不前进也不后退。该义项记录于 1905 年，是平衡意象在金属中的版本。

senses.title: Grammatical neuter: neither masculine nor feminine
senses.titleCN: 语法中性：既非阳性也非阴性
senses.definition: in grammar, of a gender that is neither masculine nor feminine
senses.definitionCN: 在语法中，指既非阳性也非阴性的性
senses.example: Latin bellum, meaning war, is a neuter noun.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语 bellum（战争）是一个中性名词。
senses.why: Latin neuter means 'neither the one nor the other of two'. Grammar applies that either-or refusal to gender, so a noun can stand outside the pair.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 neuter 意为“两者皆非”。语法把这种“两个都不是”的拒绝用在性上，于是名词可以站在这对选项之外。

senses.title: Neutral tone: plain and non-committal
senses.titleCN: 中性语气：平实、不表态
senses.definition: of language or manner, plain and without emotion, giving nothing away
senses.definitionCN: 指语言或态度平实、不带情绪，不透露立场
senses.example: She answered in a neutral tone that gave nothing away.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一种不露声色的中性语气回答。
senses.why: A neutral colour commits to no hue, and a neutral tone commits to no side. The same middle position is applied to speech.
senses.whyCN: 中性色不对任何色相表态，中性语气也不对任何一方表态。同一个“中间位置”被用到了言语上。

intro.en: Neutral is recorded in the 1540s, first in alchemy for a balance of opposing elements, and almost at once for a person who takes no side. Latin neutralis goes back to neuter 'neither the one nor the other', probably a calque of Greek oudeteros.
intro.cn: neutral 记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，最初用于炼金术中对立元素的平衡，几乎同时就用于不选边的人。拉丁语 neutralis 可追溯至 neuter“两者皆非”，很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

items.en: First recorded in the 1540s in alchemy, for a substance in which opposing elements balance, and for the sense 'not taking sides'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，用于炼金术中对立元素相衡的物质，同时也有“不选边”义。

items.en: By the 1550s the word is used of persons who do not join either party in a quarrel.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 50 年代，这个词已用于不加入争吵任何一方的人。

items.en: Latin neutralis comes from neuter 'neither the one nor the other, neither of two': ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two'. It is probably a calque of Greek oudeteros.
items.cn: 拉丁语 neutralis 来自 neuter“两者皆非、两者都不是”：ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”。它很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

items.en: The two parts are PIE *ne- 'not' and the stem behind uter 'either', which is related to English whether.
items.cn: 两个部分分别是原始印欧语 *ne-“不”与 uter“两者之一”背后的词干，后者与英语 whether 同源。

items.en: Chemistry adopts the word in the 1660s for 'neither acid nor alkaline'; the sense 'not a belligerent' follows in 1711 and the colour sense in 1821.
items.cn: 化学在 17 世纪 60 年代采用这个词，表示“非酸非碱”；“非交战国”义随后于 1711 年出现，颜色义于 1821 年出现。

items.en: The noun is recorded in the mid-15c.; mechanical neutral appears in 1905, and the neutral particle the neutron takes the word into physics.
items.cn: 名词义在 15 世纪中期已有记录；机械空挡义出现于 1905 年，而中性粒子 neutron 把这个词带进了物理学。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and scientific kinship, the second for the idea of not taking a side.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写与科学上的亲缘关系挑选，第二组按“不选边”的意思挑选。

entries.definition: grammatically neither masculine nor feminine. It is the Latin source word neuter, from which neutralis was formed.
entries.definitionCN: 语法上既非阳性也非阴性的。它就是拉丁语源词 neuter，neutralis 由它构成。

entries.definition: existing in nature, not made by people. It starts from Latin natura 'birth', not from neuter.
entries.definitionCN: 自然的；天生的。它来自拉丁语 natura“出生”，不是来自 neuter。

entries.definition: a particle with no electric charge. Its name was coined from neutral plus -on.
entries.definitionCN: 不带电的粒子。它的名字由 neutral 加 -on 造出。

entries.definition: not favouring one side unfairly. It judges fairly between parties, while neutral can also mean simply staying out.
entries.definitionCN: 公正的；不偏不倚的。它在两方之间公正判断，而 neutral 也可以只是置身事外。

entries.definition: showing no interest or concern. It describes unconcern, while neutral describes a balanced position between sides.
entries.definitionCN: 漠不关心的。它描述的是不关心，而 neutral 描述的是在两方之间的平衡位置。

entries.definition: of a state, not formally allied to any major power bloc. It is a political term, narrower than neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 不结盟的。它指国家不正式加入任何大国集团，是政治术语，范围比 neutral 窄。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: ne- plus uter inside neuter, the Latin source neutralis, and the dated scientific senses that followed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：neuter 内部的 ne- 加 uter、拉丁语来源 neutralis，以及随后有年代可查的科学义项。

normal.en: ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two' makes 'neither of the two': the middle position is built into the word.
normal.cn: ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”就是“两者皆非”：中间位置被造进了这个词里。

normal.en: Alchemy gave the first sense, a balance of opposing elements; chemistry kept the picture as neither acid nor alkaline.
normal.cn: 炼金术给了第一个义项，即对立元素的平衡；化学保留这幅画，表示非酸非碱。

normal.en: A neutral country and a neutral referee hold the same spot: outside the two sides.
normal.cn: 中立国与中立裁判站的是同一个位置：在两方之外。

normal.en: Neutral grey commits to no hue, just as a neutral tone commits to no opinion.
normal.cn: 中性灰不对任何色相表态，正如中性语气不对任何观点表态。

normal.en: A gearbox in neutral transmits nothing: the balance image appears again in metal.
normal.cn: 处于空挡的变速器什么也不传递：平衡意象又一次出现在金属里。

abstract.en: A tug-of-war rope whose red marker hangs exactly on the centre line: both teams pull, the marker stays.
abstract.cn: 拔河绳上的红布恰好停在中心线上：两队都在拉，红布不动。

abstract.en: Two arrows pushing a ball from opposite sides with equal force: the ball does not move.
abstract.cn: 两支箭头从相反方向用同样的力推一个球：球不移动。

abstract.en: A switch resting in the middle between on and off: no current, no direction, no commitment.
abstract.cn: 一个停在“开”与“关”正中的开关：没有电流、没有方向、没有承诺。

examples.en: The mediator remained neutral even when one side raised its voice.
examples.cn: 即使一方提高了嗓门，调解人仍然保持中立。

examples.en: Choose a neutral wall colour so the furniture can change later.
examples.cn: 选一种中性的墙面颜色，以后换家具也容易搭配。

examples.en: The country declared itself neutral at the start of the war.
examples.cn: 这个国家在战争开始时宣布中立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛戳」——牛站在两方中间，哪边都不戳、不顶 → neutral 中立的、中性的

root: 源自拉丁语 neutralis，来自 neuter“两者皆非”＝ ne-“不”＋ uter“两者之一”；uter 与 whether 同源，很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of neutral all come from a single position: exactly in the middle, committed to neither side. Alchemy applied it to elements, politics to parties, chemistry to acids, physics to charge, grammar to gender, and speech to tone.
sensesIntro.cn: neutral 的十个义项都来自同一个位置：恰在正中，不属于任何一边。炼金术把它用在元素上，政治用在阵营上，化学用在酸碱上，物理用在电荷上，语法用在性上，言语用在语气上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tug-of-war marker stopped exactly on the centre line.
core.cn: 核心意象：拔河绳上的标记恰好停在中心线上。

branches.en: THE BALANCED MIDDLE: opposing elements in alchemy, and opposing parties in a dispute.
branches.cn: 平衡的中间：炼金术中的对立元素，以及争端中的对立两方。

branches.en: SCIENTIFIC NEUTRALITY: neither acid nor alkaline, and no net electric charge.
branches.cn: 科学上的中性：非酸非碱，以及净电荷为零。

branches.en: THE UNCOMMITTED PARTY: a state outside a war, and the person or place chosen to host talks.
branches.cn: 未承诺的一方：战争之外的国家，以及被选作会谈地点的人或地方。

branches.en: THE QUIET SURFACE: low-saturation colour, and a tone that gives nothing away.
branches.cn: 安静的表层：低彩度的颜色，以及不透露立场的语气。

branches.en: NEITHER ENGAGED NOR EITHER: a gearbox in neutral, and a grammatical gender outside the pair.
branches.cn: 既不咬合也不属于任何一边：空挡的变速器，以及跳出阴阳两性的语法中性。

intro.en: Neutral is Latin neutralis plus -al, from neuter. English builds neutrality, neutrally, neutralize, neutralization, neutralist and neutralism, and the same stem gives neuter and neutron.
intro.cn: neutral 是拉丁语 neutralis 加 -al，源自 neuter。英语构造出 neutrality、neutrally、neutralize、neutralization、neutralist、neutralism，同一词干还给出 neuter 与 neutron。

latinIntro.en: Latin neutralis 'of the neuter gender, neutral' comes from neuter 'neither of two', itself ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 neutralis“中性的、中立的”来自 neuter“两者皆非”，后者由 ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”构成。

items.meaning: taking no side; neither one nor the other
items.meaningCN: 中立的；中性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The village stayed neutral during the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 争端期间这个村子保持中立。

items.meaning: the state of taking no side
items.meaningCN: 中立；中性（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The treaty guaranteed the neutrality of the port.
items.exampleCN: 条约保障了该港口的中立地位。

items.meaning: in a non-committal way
items.meaningCN: 中立地；平淡地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She described the quarrel neutrally, naming no culprit.
items.exampleCN: 她中立地描述了这场争吵，没有指名任何一方。

items.meaning: to cancel the effect of something
items.meaningCN: 使中和；抵消（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The base neutralizes the acid almost instantly.
items.exampleCN: 碱几乎立刻中和了酸。

items.meaning: the act of cancelling or balancing
items.meaningCN: 中和作用；抵消（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The neutralization produced ordinary salt and water.
items.exampleCN: 中和反应生成了普通的盐和水。

items.meaning: a supporter of political neutrality
items.meaningCN: 中立主义者（-ist 构成人名名词）
items.example: The neutralists opposed joining either alliance.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义者反对加入任何一个联盟。

items.meaning: the policy of staying outside rival blocs
items.meaningCN: 中立主义（-ism 构成主张名词）
items.example: Neutralism shaped the country's foreign policy.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义塑造了该国的外交政策。

items.meaning: grammatically neither masculine nor feminine
items.meaningCN: 中性的；既非阳也非阴（ne-“不”+ uter“两者之一”）
items.example: The Latin word for leaf is neuter.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语中“叶子”这个词是中性名词。

items.meaning: a particle with no electric charge
items.meaningCN: 中子（neutral 加粒子后缀 -on，指不带电的粒子）
items.example: A neutron passes through the electric field undeflected.
items.exampleCN: 中子穿过电场时不发生偏转。

items.meaning: something that cancels an effect
items.meaningCN: 中和剂；抵消物（-er 构成施动物名词）
items.example: The lab keeps a neutralizer beside every acid bath.
items.exampleCN: 实验室在每个酸槽旁都放一瓶中和剂。

latinEntries.meaning: neither the one nor the other

latinEntries.meaningCN: 两者之一（与英语 whether 同源）

definition_en: in spite of that; however; used to introduce a statement that stands despite what came before
core_image: 门上挂着“禁止进入”的牌子，人还是推门走了进去
scene: The trail is closed and half flooded; nevertheless, a hiker steps past the sign and walks on.
sceneCN: 这里 nevertheless 是「尽管如此、仍然」（第 1 个义项：让步之后仍然成立）；句意：步道已经封闭、有一半被水淹，尽管如此，一名徒步者还是绕过告示牌继续往前走。图中可辨识物件：封闭告示牌、积水步道、徒步者的登山杖、黄黑警示带。

pos.zh: 然而；尽管如此；不过（连接性副词，承接前文并转折）

collocations.zh: 尽管如此，事实仍然不变

derivatives.zh: 尽管如此（同构的并列复合词，用 none 代替 never）
从不；决不（构词成分，此处原义为“一点也不”）
曾经；无论何时（never 的第二成分）
更少的；更少地（构词成分，比较级）
除非（同出 less 的复合连词）
减少；减轻（less 加 -en 构成的动词）

senses.title: In spite of that: opening a sentence against expectation
senses.titleCN: 尽管如此：开门见山地逆着预期说
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to say that what follows is true in spite of what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，表示接下来的内容尽管有前文所说的情况仍然成立
senses.example: The hotel was full. Nevertheless, we found a room nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆客满了。尽管如此，我们还是在附近找到了一间房。
senses.why: Nevertheless is never plus the less, literally 'not any the less'. What came before does not make the next statement any smaller, so the sentence opens by refusing to be reduced.
senses.whyCN: nevertheless 是 never 加 the less，字面是“一点也不因此减少”。前文并没有让后一句变小，所以这个句子一开口就拒绝被削减。

senses.title: Joining two clauses after a semicolon
senses.titleCN: 用分号连接两个小句
senses.definition: used after a semicolon to link two clauses and mark the second as a contrast
senses.definitionCN: 用于分号之后连接两个小句，并标记后一句为转折
senses.example: The evidence was thin; nevertheless, the jury convicted.
senses.exampleCN: 证据薄弱；尽管如此，陪审团仍判定有罪。
senses.why: As a conjunctive adverb it carries the contrast across the punctuation. The 'not any the less' still measures the second clause against the first.
senses.whyCN: 作为连接性副词，它把转折跨过标点带过去。“一点也不因此减少”仍在用前一句来衡量后一句。

senses.title: After but: the doubled contrast
senses.titleCN: 跟在 but 之后：双重的转折
senses.definition: used with but to add emphasis, as in 'cheap but nevertheless good'
senses.definitionCN: 与 but 连用以加强转折，如 cheap but nevertheless good
senses.example: The plan was expensive but nevertheless worth every penny.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划很贵，但尽管如此，每一分钱都值得。
senses.why: But already turns the sentence; nevertheless adds that the earlier fact does not reduce the later one. The two markers reinforce rather than contradict each other.
senses.whyCN: but 已经让句子转向；nevertheless 再补上一层：前面的事实并不能削减后面的事实。两个标记是相互加强，而不是相互矛盾。

senses.title: At the end: a trailing afterthought
senses.titleCN: 放在句尾：事后的补一句
senses.definition: placed at the end of a clause to add a delayed contrast, often after a pause
senses.definitionCN: 放在小句末尾，补充一个迟来的转折，常出现在停顿之后
senses.example: It was a foolish plan. He went ahead, nevertheless.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个愚蠢的计划。他还是照做了，尽管如此。
senses.why: The word can trail because the comparison is still live: the action is measured against the warning and is 'none the less' for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以拖在句尾，因为比较仍然有效：行动相对于警告被衡量，而它“并未因此减少”。

senses.title: Academic concession: grant the objection, keep the claim
senses.titleCN: 学术让步：承认异议，保留论点
senses.definition: used in argument to admit a limitation and still maintain the main claim
senses.definitionCN: 用于论证中，承认某项局限，同时仍然坚持主要论点
senses.example: The sample is small; nevertheless, the result is suggestive.
senses.exampleCN: 样本很小；尽管如此，这一结果仍有提示意义。
senses.why: The concession lowers the claim's strength, and nevertheless says the claim is not lowered by that amount. It is the written form of 'none the less'.
senses.whyCN: 让步降低了论点的强度，而 nevertheless 说论点并没有因此降低那么多。它就是书面语里的“none the less”。

senses.title: Personal admission: I knew, and did it anyway
senses.titleCN: 个人承认：我知道，可我还是做了
senses.definition: used to admit a fault or risk and still report the action taken
senses.definitionCN: 用于承认过错或风险，却仍然陈述已经采取的行动
senses.example: I knew the risk; nevertheless, I signed.
senses.exampleCN: 我知道有风险；尽管如此，我还是签了。
senses.why: Here the first clause is self-criticism. Nevertheless refuses to let the admission cancel the act, so the person owns both at once.
senses.whyCN: 这里前一句是自我批评。nevertheless 不让这份承认取消行动，于是这个人同时承认了两件事。

senses.title: Formal register: the steady voice of statutes
senses.titleCN: 正式语体：法条里沉稳的声音
senses.definition: used in legal, official, and technical prose as a formal alternative to 'but' or 'however'
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、公文与技术写作中作为 but 或 however 的正式替代
senses.example: The notice was defective; nevertheless, it had legal effect.
senses.exampleCN: 该通知存在瑕疵；尽管如此，它仍具有法律效力。
senses.why: The compound is long and steady, and its 'none the less' logic suits rules that survive exceptions. Formal prose prefers it to a bare but.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词长而稳，其“并未减少”的逻辑正合那些在例外之后仍然存活的规则。正式写作偏爱它，而不是光秃秃的 but。

senses.title: Narrative: obstacles listed, outcome unchanged
senses.titleCN: 叙事：障碍列举完，结果不变
senses.definition: used in storytelling after a list of difficulties to show the result still happened
senses.definitionCN: 在叙事中用于列举困难之后，表示结果仍然发生
senses.example: Rain, delays and lost luggage — nevertheless, they arrived on time.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨、延误、行李丢失——尽管如此，他们还是准时到了。
senses.why: Each obstacle would normally count against the outcome. The word gathers them and says the outcome is none the less for all of them.
senses.whyCN: 每一项障碍通常都会对结果不利。这个词把它们收拢起来，说结果并没有因为这一切而减少。

senses.title: Emphatic: after an extreme list, the result still stands
senses.titleCN: 强调：极端情况之后，结果仍然成立
senses.definition: used after the strongest possible objection to insist that the result stands
senses.definitionCN: 用于最强的反对意见之后，坚持结果仍然成立
senses.example: Every forecast said failure; nevertheless, the launch succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 所有预测都说会失败；尽管如此，发射还是成功了。
senses.why: The stronger the objection, the more the 'not any the less' has to do. Here the word is close to 'against all of it'.
senses.whyCN: 反对越强，“一点也不因此减少”要做的功就越大。这里的词义接近“对抗这一切”。

senses.title: The fixed frame: it is nevertheless true that
senses.titleCN: 固定框架：it is nevertheless true that
senses.definition: used in the frame 'it is nevertheless true that' to affirm a fact after doubt has been raised
senses.definitionCN: 用于 it is nevertheless true that 这一框架，在被质疑之后仍然肯定某一事实
senses.example: It is nevertheless true that the method saved lives.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管如此，这个方法确实救过人命，这一点是真的。
senses.why: The frame places truth itself on the far side of the contrast: whatever was argued, the fact is none the less true.
senses.whyCN: 这个框架把“真”本身放到转折的另一边：无论前面争论了什么，事实并未因此而不真。

intro.en: Nevertheless began as the phrase never the less, written neuer þe lesse in the early 14c. and joined into one word by the mid-14c. Its never does not mean 'never' but 'not at all, none the', as in never the wiser.
intro.cn: nevertheless 起初是短语 never the less，14 世纪早期写作 neuer þe lesse，到 14 世纪中期合成一词。其中的 never 不是“永不”，而是“一点也不、none the”，如 never the wiser。

items.en: First recorded in the early 14c. as the phrase neuer þe lesse, still written in separate parts.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪早期，写作短语 neuer þe lesse，各部分仍分开书写。

items.en: By the mid-14c. the parts are joined as neuerþeles, and the word begins to work as a single adverb.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪中期，各部分合成 neuerþeles，这个词开始作为单一副词使用。

items.en: Middle English also had neverthelater, never-less, ner-the-less, never-later and not-the-less, all built on the same 'none the less' pattern.
items.cn: 中古英语还有 neverthelater、never-less、ner-the-less、never-later、not-the-less 等变体，都建立在同一个“none the less”模式上。

items.en: Never comes from Old English næfre, itself ne 'not' plus æfre 'ever'.
items.cn: never 来自古英语 næfre，本身由 ne“不”加 æfre“曾经”构成。

items.en: Modern English keeps nevertheless beside nonetheless; the two are parallel compounds, one with never and one with none.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nevertheless 与 nonetheless 并存；两者是并列复合词，一个用 never，一个用 none。

note.en: The first group shares the never-the-less shape or its parts, the second shares the contrastive meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 never-the-less 的结构或其组成部分，第二组共享转折的词义。

entries.definition: in spite of that. It is built exactly like nevertheless but with none instead of never, and the two are interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此。它的构造与 nevertheless 完全相同，只是用 none 代替 never，两者可以互换。

entries.definition: the older phrase written in separate words. It shows the literal parts: never, the, less.
entries.definitionCN: 分开书写的较早短语。它显示了这个词的字面成分：never、the、less。

entries.definition: an obsolete variant of nevertheless, built with later instead of less. It shows how freely the pattern was varied.
entries.definitionCN: nevertheless 的废弃变体，用 later 而不是 less。它说明这个模式当年被替换得多么自由。

entries.definition: in whatever way, or used to introduce a contrast. It is the general-purpose connector, while nevertheless is heavier and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 无论如何；然而。它是通用连接词，而 nevertheless 更重、更正式。

entries.definition: in spite of; despite. It often works as a preposition or a formal connector, and is even heavier than nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管；虽然。它常作介词或正式连接词，比 nevertheless 还要重。

entries.definition: in spite of that, used in speech. It carries the same turn but sounds conversational rather than written.
entries.definitionCN: 即使如此。它带有同样的转折，但听起来是口语而非书面语。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: never here means 'not at all', less is a comparative, and the Middle English variants all repeat the same pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：这里的 never 意为“一点也不”，less 是比较级，而中古英语的各种变体都重复同一个模式。

normal.en: Never in this word is not 'never': it means 'not at all, none the', as in never the wiser or never the worse.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 never 不是“永不”：它意为“一点也不、none the”，如 never the wiser、never the worse。

normal.en: the less is a comparative. Together the parts say 'not any the less', which is why the later clause is not reduced.
normal.cn: the less 是比较级。合起来说“一点也不因此减少”，这正是后一句没有被削减的原因。

normal.en: Middle English had neverthelater, never-less, ner-the-less and not-the-less, all variations on the same comparison.
normal.cn: 中古英语有 neverthelater、never-less、ner-the-less、not-the-less，都是同一个比较结构的变体。

normal.en: Nonetheless is the twin: same building plan, with none instead of never.
normal.cn: nonetheless 是它的双胞胎：同样的建筑图纸，只用 none 代替 never。

normal.en: But nevertheless is a standard frame: but turns the sentence, nevertheless insists nothing was lost in the turn.
normal.cn: but nevertheless 是标准框架：but 让句子转向，nevertheless 坚持这次转向没有损失任何东西。

abstract.en: A door marked NO ENTRY, already pushed half open: the warning is real, and the step is still taken.
abstract.cn: 一扇写着“禁止入内”的门已被推开一半：警告是真的，脚步还是迈了出去。

abstract.en: A line that bends at an obstacle and then continues in the same direction: the bend does not shorten the road.
abstract.cn: 一条线在障碍处弯了一下，然后继续朝同一方向走：弯折并没有让路变短。

abstract.en: A hand pressing down on a box while another hand still lifts it: the weight is counted, and the lift still happens.
abstract.cn: 一只手向下压箱子，另一只手仍把它抬起：重量被算进去了，抬起仍然发生。

examples.en: The instructions were unclear; nevertheless, the team finished on time.
examples.cn: 说明不清楚；尽管如此，团队还是按时完成了。

examples.en: He was warned about the ice, but nevertheless he walked out onto the lake.
examples.cn: 有人警告过他冰面危险，但尽管如此，他还是走上了湖面。

examples.en: It is nevertheless true that the old bridge has carried the town's traffic for a century.
examples.cn: 尽管如此，这座老桥确实已经承载了小镇一个世纪的交通，这一点是真的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那我也赖着」——尽管被赶、被劝，那我也赖着不走 → nevertheless 尽管如此、仍然

root: 由 never“一点也不、none the”＋ the ＋ less（比较级）构成的复合副词，14 世纪早期写作 neuer þe lesse；never 来自古英语 næfre＝ ne“不”＋ æfre“曾经”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of nevertheless all carry one comparison: whatever was said, the next statement is 'none the less'. The word changes position and register, from sentence opening to trailing afterthought, from academic concession to legal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: nevertheless 的十个义项都带着同一个比较：无论前面说了什么，后一句都“并未因此减少”。这个词改变的是位置与语体，从句首到句尾补语，从学术让步到法律文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed sign on a door that is opened anyway.
core.cn: 核心意象：门上的封闭告示，而门还是被推开了。

branches.en: SENTENCE POSITIONS: opening a new sentence, and joining two clauses after a semicolon.
branches.cn: 句子位置：开启一个新句子，以及在分号后连接两个小句。

branches.en: DOUBLED AND TRAILING: after but for extra emphasis, and at the end as a delayed afterthought.
branches.cn: 加倍与拖尾：跟在 but 后加强语气，以及放在句尾作迟来的补语。

branches.en: PERSONAL AND ARGUMENTATIVE CONCESSION: granting a limitation, and admitting a fault while acting anyway.
branches.cn: 论证与个人的让步：承认局限，以及承认过错却仍然行动。

branches.en: REGISTER AND NARRATIVE: the steady voice of statutes, and obstacles listed before an unchanged outcome.
branches.cn: 语体与叙事：法条沉稳的声音，以及列举障碍后结果依旧。

branches.en: MAXIMUM RESISTANCE: after the strongest objection, and in the fixed frame it is nevertheless true that.
branches.cn: 最大阻力：最强反对之后，以及 it is nevertheless true that 这一固定框架。

intro.en: Nevertheless is a compound, not a suffixed word: never plus the plus less. English keeps the same plan in nonetheless, and the parts survive separately in never, ever, less, unless and lessen.
intro.cn: nevertheless 是复合词，不是加后缀的词：never 加 the 加 less。英语用同一图纸造出 nonetheless，而各成分分别活在 never、ever、less、unless、lessen 中。

latinIntro.en: Nevertheless is Germanic. The Latin entries below are counterparts for contrast: nihilominus and tamen both mean 'nevertheless', and minus supplies 'less'.
latinIntro.cn: nevertheless 属日耳曼语。下面的拉丁词是对照用的对应词：nihilominus 与 tamen 都表示“尽管如此”，minus 提供“更少”。

items.meaning: in spite of that; none the less
items.meaningCN: 尽管如此；并未因此减少（never“一点也不”+ the + less 比较级）
items.example: The road was closed; nevertheless, we reached the village.
items.exampleCN: 道路封闭了；尽管如此，我们还是到了村子。

items.meaning: in spite of that
items.meaningCN: 尽管如此（none“一点也不”+ the + less，与 nevertheless 同构）
items.example: The sample was small; nonetheless, the pattern was clear.
items.exampleCN: 样本虽小；尽管如此，规律仍然清楚。

items.meaning: not at any time
items.meaningCN: 从不；决不（ne“不”+ æfre“曾经”）
items.example: He never spoke of the accident again.
items.exampleCN: 他再也没有提起那次事故。

items.meaning: at any time
items.meaningCN: 曾经；无论何时（never 的第二成分）
items.example: Have you ever seen the tide come in this fast?
items.exampleCN: 你见过潮水涨得这么快的景象吗？

items.meaning: a smaller amount; not as much
items.meaningCN: 更少的；更少地（little 的比较级）
items.example: This route takes less time than the motorway.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线比高速公路花的时间更少。

items.meaning: except if
items.meaningCN: 除非（由 on lesse“在少于……的条件下”演变而来）
items.example: We will go unless it rains.
items.exampleCN: 除非下雨，否则我们就去。

items.meaning: to make or become smaller
items.meaningCN: 减少；减轻（less + -en 构成动词）
items.example: The medicine lessened the pain within an hour.
items.exampleCN: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。

items.meaning: smaller or less important
items.meaningCN: 较小的；次要的（less 再加 -er 的历史双重比较级）
items.example: The lesser of the two risks was still serious.
items.exampleCN: 两个风险中较小的那个仍然很严重。

items.meaning: never again
items.meaningCN: 再也不（never + more，文学用语）
items.example: The raven said, 'Nevermore.'
items.exampleCN: 那只渡鸦说：“再也不了。”

items.meaning: seemingly without end
items.meaningCN: 永无止境的（never + ending，复合形容词）
items.example: The repairs felt like a never-ending task.
items.exampleCN: 这些修缮活像一项永无止境的任务。

definition_zh: 规范；准则；常态；标准；平均值
definition_en: a standard, rule, or usual pattern by which things are measured or judged
core_image: 木匠手里的直角尺：所有木板都要与它对齐
scene: A carpenter lays a steel square on a plank and uses it as the norm for every corner he cuts.
sceneCN: 这里 norm 是「量度所依的规矩、标准」（第 1 个义项：用来量度和判断的准则）；句意：木匠把钢制直角尺放在木板上，把它当作每个转角的准则，切割前逐一比对。图中可辨识物件：直角尺、木板、铅笔线、锯子、木屑。

pos.zh: 规范；准则；标准
常态；惯常做法
（统计）平均值；基准量

senses.title: The Carpenter's Square: the rule things are measured against
senses.titleCN: 木工尺：万物对齐的规矩
senses.definition: a standard, pattern, or model used to measure or judge something
senses.definitionCN: 用来量度或判断事物的标准、范式或模型
senses.example: The team treated the first drawing as the norm for every later copy.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把最初的图纸当作此后每一份复制品的标准。
senses.why: Latin norma was the carpenter's square, the tool that tests whether a corner is true. From the tool itself came the abstract sense 'a rule or model to measure by', the sense Coleridge recorded in 1821.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 norma 是木工尺，用来检验角是否方正。从这件工具直接引出抽象义“量度所依的规矩或范式”，也就是柯勒律治 1821 年记录的那个义项。

senses.title: What Most People Do: the usual pattern
senses.titleCN: 多数人的做法：惯常模式
senses.definition: the usual or typical way of behaving, especially when most people accept it
senses.definitionCN: 通常或典型的行为方式，尤指多数人接受的方式
senses.example: In this office, arriving before nine has become the norm.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个办公室，九点前到岗已成为常态。
senses.why: Once a rule is shared, whatever follows it repeatedly looks like the rule in action. The standard becomes the ordinary case, so norm comes to mean the usual pattern.
senses.whyCN: 一旦规矩被共享，反复照着它做的样子就像是规矩本身在运行。标准于是变成普通情形，norm 也就有了“惯常模式”义。

senses.title: An Unwritten Law: a group's shared expectation
senses.titleCN: 不成文法：群体共享的期待
senses.definition: an accepted standard of behaviour that a group expects its members to follow
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体期待成员遵守的、被认可的行为标准
senses.example: Every culture has norms about how close you may stand when talking.
senses.exampleCN: 每种文化都有关于交谈时能站多近的规范。
senses.why: The measuring square is social here: the group lays it against each member's conduct. What fits the square is approved; what falls outside is deviant.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺子是社会的：群体把它贴在每个成员的行为上。对齐尺子的被认可，偏离尺子的被视为越轨。

senses.title: The Average Line: a statistical norm
senses.titleCN: 平均线：统计上的常模
senses.definition: the average or typical level of a measured quantity in a population
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中某项被测数量的平均或典型水平
senses.example: The test scores were compared with the national norm for that age group.
senses.exampleCN: 这些测验分数与同年龄组的全国常模作了比较。
senses.why: Statistics draws one line through many scattered measurements. That line is the measure of the group, so the old 'rule' becomes the average value.
senses.whyCN: 统计学在许多散乱的测量值中画出一条线。这条线就是群体的量度，于是古老的“规矩”变成平均值。

senses.title: The Line Others Must Meet: a benchmark
senses.titleCN: 他人须达到的线：基准
senses.definition: a level of performance or achievement used as a standard for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 用作比较标准的表现或成就水平
senses.example: Her time in the race set a new norm for the club.
senses.exampleCN: 她的比赛用时为俱乐部立下了新的基准。
senses.why: If the square decides what counts as straight, it also decides what counts as good enough. A measured result can therefore be held up as the norm others must match.
senses.whyCN: 如果尺子决定什么算直，它也就决定什么算达标。因此一个测得的成绩可以被举为他人必须对齐的基准。

senses.title: Size in Mathematics: the length of a vector
senses.titleCN: 数学中的大小：向量的模
senses.definition: in mathematics, a function that assigns a size or length to a vector or a space
senses.definitionCN: 数学中为向量或空间指定大小、长度的函数
senses.example: The norm of the vector is the square root of the sum of its squared components.
senses.exampleCN: 这个向量的模是其各分量平方和的平方根。
senses.why: Mathematics keeps the oldest meaning most literally: a norm is the rule that tells you how large an object is. Size itself is measured by that rule.
senses.whyCN: 数学最字面地保留了最古老的含义：norm 就是告诉你一个对象有多大的那把尺。大小由这把尺来量。

senses.title: The Accepted Way of Speaking: a linguistic standard
senses.titleCN: 被认可的说话方式：语言规范
senses.definition: the standard form of a language, or the accepted usage in a community of speakers
senses.definitionCN: 语言的标准形式，或某个说话群体中被认可的用法
senses.example: Dictionaries record usage; they do not always prescribe the norm.
senses.exampleCN: 词典记录用法，并不总是规定规范。
senses.why: Language also has a straight edge: grammar and spelling are checked against an accepted pattern. What fits that pattern is called the norm.
senses.whyCN: 语言也有一把直尺：语法和拼写要对着被认可的范式检查。符合这个范式的就叫规范。

senses.title: A Rule of Conduct: the ethical norm
senses.titleCN: 行为规则：伦理规范
senses.definition: a principle of right conduct that guides or judges moral behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指导或评判道德行为的正当行为原则
senses.example: The ethical norm of informed consent shapes modern medical research.
senses.exampleCN: 知情同意的伦理规范塑造了现代医学研究。
senses.why: The social square becomes a moral one: actions are laid against a principle and judged straight or crooked. That principle is the norm.
senses.whyCN: 社会的尺子变成道德的尺子：行为被放在原则旁边，判为端直或歪斜。这条原则就是规范。

senses.title: The Fixed Specification: a technical standard
senses.titleCN: 固定规格：技术标准
senses.definition: an official or technical specification that a product or process must meet
senses.definitionCN: 产品或流程必须达到的官方或技术规格
senses.example: The bolts were manufactured to a norm agreed by the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这些螺栓按行业商定的标准制造。
senses.why: In industry the measuring tool becomes written down: the rule is fixed in numbers so that every copy matches. The norm is then a specification.
senses.whyCN: 在工业里，量具被写成了文字：规矩固定为数字，让每一件复制品都对齐。此时 norm 就是规格。

intro.en: Norm entered English in 1821 through French from Latin norma, the carpenter's square. The tool's name became the abstract word for a standard, while norma's deeper origin is unknown.
intro.cn: norm 于 1821 年经法语从拉丁语 norma（木工尺）进入英语。工具的名字变成了 abstract 意义上的“标准”，而 norma 更深层的来源不明。

items.en: Latin norma was already used in English for a carpenter's square; in the 18th century Lacaille also gave the name Norma to a small southern constellation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 norma 在 17 世纪 70 年代已被英语用来指木工尺；18 世纪拉卡伊还把 Norma 用作南天一个小星座的名字。
