senses.title: The Object in the Mind: the 1610s philosophical sense
senses.titleCN: 心中的对象：17 世纪初的哲学义
senses.definition: in 1610s philosophy, existing as perceived or thought, ideal, representative, or phenomenal, as opposed to subjective or formal
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪初哲学中，指作为被感知或被思考之物而存在的、观念的、表象的、现象的，与 subjective 或 formal 相对
senses.example: In the old debate, pain was called objective when considered as a thought rather than a bodily state.
senses.exampleCN: 在那场古老争论中，痛苦被当作思想而非身体状态来看时，被称为 objective。
senses.why: The word was built from objectum, 'a thing put before the mind'. In the 1610s that thing was still inside the mind, so objective meant 'existing as an object of thought'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 objectum“被摆到心智面前的东西”构成。17 世纪初，这东西还在心智之内，所以 objective 意为“作为思想对象而存在”。

senses.title: The Real Thing Outside: independent of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心外实物：不依赖心智而存在
senses.definition: real and existing independently of the mind, belonging to the object of knowledge rather than to the observer
senses.definitionCN: 真实存在、不依赖心智的，属于认知对象而非观察者的
senses.example: The mountain has an objective existence whether or not anyone looks at it.
senses.exampleCN: 无论是否有人看它，这座山都客观存在。
senses.why: From the mid-17th century the 'object' was pushed outside: what is objective is what belongs to the thing known, not to the knower. The sense almost reverses the older one.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪中期起，“对象”被推到心智之外：objective 的东西属于被认识的事物，而不属于认识者。这个义项几乎翻转了旧义。

senses.title: Without a Personal Lens: impartial
senses.titleCN: 不戴个人镜片：不偏不倚
senses.definition: not influenced by personal feelings, interests, or bias when judging
senses.definitionCN: 判断时不受个人情感、利益或偏见影响
senses.example: A judge must remain objective even when the case is emotionally charged.
senses.exampleCN: 即使案件牵动情绪，法官也必须保持客观。
senses.why: If truth belongs to the object, the observer should stop adding private colour. The 18th-century sense, strengthened through German translations, names that disciplined detachment.
senses.whyCN: 如果真相属于对象，观察者就该停止添加私人色彩。18 世纪经德语译介强化的义项，命名的正是这种克制的抽离。

senses.title: What the Evidence Shows: fact-based
senses.titleCN: 证据所示：以事实为依据
senses.definition: based on observable facts and evidence that others can check
senses.definitionCN: 建立在他人可以核查的可观察事实与证据之上
senses.example: The report gives an objective account of the accident, with times and measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用时间和测量数据，对事故作了客观陈述。
senses.why: An account is objective when it stays with what was put before the senses: times, measurements, records. Evidence replaces opinion as the measure.
senses.whyCN: 当陈述停留在摆在感官之前的东西——时间、测量、记录——它就是客观的。证据取代意见成为量尺。

senses.title: The Point to Be Taken: a military objective
senses.titleCN: 要夺取的点：军事目标
senses.definition: a place or position that an army aims to capture or hold, from which the general noun use grew
senses.definitionCN: 军队意图夺取或守住的地点或阵地，名词的一般用法由此而来
senses.example: The hill was the objective of the night attack.
senses.exampleCN: 那座山头是夜袭的目标。
senses.why: Military language used objective for the point set before the force, the thing to be taken. The target on the map is literally 'the object put in front'.
senses.whyCN: 军事语言用 objective 指摆在部队前方的点，即要夺取的东西。地图上的目标字面上就是“被摆在前面的对象”。

senses.title: The Aim: a goal to reach
senses.titleCN: 目的：要到达的标的
senses.definition: a goal or aim that a person or organization works toward
senses.definitionCN: 个人或组织努力要达到的目标
senses.example: Our main objective is to cut waiting times by half.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的主要目标是把等待时间减少一半。
senses.why: Once the military target became general, any planned end point could be an objective: something placed ahead of you that guides effort.
senses.whyCN: 军事目标一旦泛化，任何计划中的终点都可以叫 objective：一个摆在你前方、引导努力的东西。

senses.title: The Lens Facing the Object
senses.titleCN: 朝向物体的镜片：物镜
senses.definition: in optics, the lens or lens system nearest the object being viewed, as in a microscope or telescope
senses.definitionCN: 光学中离被观察物体最近的那片透镜或透镜组，如显微镜或望远镜的物镜
senses.example: Clean the objective before examining the slide.
senses.exampleCN: 检查玻片前先清洁物镜。
senses.why: The optical objective is the lens turned toward the object, not toward the eye. The same 'thing before you' image is used in a physical instrument.
senses.whyCN: 光学物镜是朝向物体、而不是朝向眼睛的那片镜片。同一个“摆在面前的东西”的意象被用在一件实体仪器上。

senses.title: The Object Case: grammar
senses.titleCN: 宾格：语法术语
senses.definition: in grammar, the case of a noun or pronoun that is the object of a verb or preposition
senses.definitionCN: 语法中名词或代词作动词或介词宾语时的格
senses.example: In 'she saw him', him is in the objective case.
senses.exampleCN: 在 she saw him 中，him 是宾格。
senses.why: Grammar names the receiver of the action the object. The objective case is simply the form a word takes when it stands as the object before the verb.
senses.whyCN: 语法把动作的承受者称为 object。宾格就是当一个词作为动词的宾语出现时所取的形式。

senses.title: Description Without Interpretation
senses.titleCN: 不带解释的描述：客观呈现
senses.definition: presenting what can be seen or measured without adding interpretation, as in objective reporting or photography
senses.definitionCN: 只呈现可见或可测的内容而不添加解释，如客观报道或客观摄影
senses.example: The photographer took an objective record of the building before demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在拆除前对建筑作了客观记录。
senses.why: The final extension keeps the observer out of the frame. What is recorded is the object as it stands, with no story laid over it.
senses.whyCN: 最后的延伸把观察者请出画面。被记录的是对象本来的样子，上面没有叠加任何故事。

intro.en: Objective is object plus -ive. Object came from Latin obiectum 'thing put before', and objective first meant 'existing as an object of thought' before its sense moved outside the mind to 'real' and then to 'impartial'.
intro.cn: objective 是 object 加 -ive。object 来自拉丁语 obiectum“被摆到面前的东西”，而 objective 最初指“作为思想对象而存在”，后来移出心智，变成“真实的”，再变成“不偏不倚的”。

items.en: First used as a philosophical term meaning 'as perceived or thought; ideal; representative; phenomenal', opposed to subjective or formal.
items.cn: 最初作哲学术语，意为“被感知或被思考的；观念的；表象的；现象的”，与 subjective 或 formal 相对。

items.en: The sense 'belonging to the real object of knowledge, real' appears, in contrast with subjective; the meaning almost reverses the earlier one.
items.cn: 出现“属于认知的实在对象、真实的”义，与 subjective 相对；含义几乎翻转了早先的义项。

items.en: The modern sense 'unbiased, not shaped by personal feeling' is strengthened through German philosophical translations.
items.cn: 现代义“客观的、不带偏见的”经德语哲学译介而强化。

items.en: Formed on medieval Latin objectivus, used by Duns Scotus, from objectum 'thing put before'.
items.cn: 按中世纪拉丁语 objectivus 构成，邓斯·司各脱曾使用，出自 objectum“被摆到面前的东西”。

items.en: Objectum is the neuter noun use of obiectus, past participle of obicere 'to throw before': ob 'in front of, towards, against' plus iacere 'to throw' (PIE *ye- 'to throw, impel').
items.cn: objectum 是 obiectus 的中性名词化；obiectus 为 obicere“投到前面”的过去分词：ob“在前、朝向、对着”+ iacere“投、掷”（原始印欧语 *ye-“投、推”）。

items.en: The noun 'objective' meaning a target comes from military usage, the point set before a force; the general sense 'goal' followed. Object itself dates from late 14c.
items.cn: 名词 objective 的“目标”义来自军事用语，即摆在部队前方的点；泛化的“目的”义随后出现。object 本身则始于 14 世纪晚期。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the object family and its -ive neighbours; the near-meaning group holds words that overlap with only part of objective.
note.cn: 形近组留在 object 词族及其 -ive 邻词内；近义组是只与 objective 部分义项重叠的词。

entries.definition: a thing that can be seen or touched, or something opposed. Objective is built from it, but the stress and the noun-verb split differ.
entries.definitionCN: 可见可触的物体，或反对的对象。objective 由它构成，但重音和名词／动词分工不同。

entries.definition: a statement of disagreement. It comes from object as a verb 'to oppose', not from objective.
entries.definitionCN: 反对的意见。它来自动词 object“反对”，而不是来自 objective。

entries.definition: a word that describes a noun. It shares the -ive ending and the Latin iacere 'throw' root, but its prefix is ad-, not ob-.
entries.definitionCN: 描述名词的词。它同样以 -ive 结尾，也含拉丁语 iacere“投”的词根，但前缀是 ad-，不是 ob-。

entries.definition: not favouring one side over another. It stresses fairness between parties, while objective stresses independence from one's own feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方。它强调各方之间的公平，objective 强调独立于自己的情感。

entries.definition: free from prejudice or a settled leaning. It is close to objective but names the absence of bias rather than the presence of facts.
entries.definitionCN: 没有偏见或既定倾向。它接近 objective，但说的是“没有偏见”，而不是“依据事实”。

entries.definition: based on facts. It covers only the evidence sense of objective and says nothing about being a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 以事实为依据的。它只覆盖 objective 的证据义，与“目标”义无关。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: objectum is ob- 'before' plus iacere 'to throw', and objective is object plus -ive. The 1610s and modern senses are a recorded reversal, not an invented story.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：objectum 是 ob-“在前”加 iacere“投”，objective 是 object 加 -ive。17 世纪初义与现代义是有记录的翻转，不是编造的故事。

normal.en: Objectum is ob- 'in front of' plus iacere 'to throw': a thing thrown before the mind or the eyes.
normal.cn: objectum 是 ob-“在前”加 iacere“投”：被投到心智或视线之前的东西。

normal.en: Objective is simply object plus -ive: 'relating to the object put before you'.
normal.cn: objective 就是 object 加 -ive：与“摆在你面前的对象”相关的。

normal.en: The 1610s sense meant 'in the mind'; the modern sense moved outside the mind to 'real'. The word reversed direction.
normal.cn: 17 世纪初的义项指“在心中的”；现代义移到心外，指“真实的”。这个词转了个方向。

normal.en: Objection and objective share object but pull opposite ways: one throws something against, the other looks at what is before.
normal.cn: objection 与 objective 都含 object，却朝相反方向拉：一个把东西扔过去反对，一个只看面前的东西。

normal.en: A military objective is the literal point set before a force; the everyday 'goal' grew from that target.
normal.cn: 军事 objective 是字面上摆在部队前方的点；日常的“目标”义从那个靶点长出来。

abstract.en: Picture an object alone under a lamp: the table, the wall and the observer all fall into shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下只有一件东西：桌子、墙和观察者都落进阴影。

abstract.en: The observer steps back until their own shadow leaves the frame; that is the move from subjective to objective.
abstract.cn: 观察者后退，直到自己的影子离开画面；这就是从主观到客观的那一步。

abstract.en: Move the same object onto a map and it becomes a target: objective is now the point to be reached.
abstract.cn: 把同一件东西移到地图上，它就成了靶点：objective 此时是要到达的点。

examples.en: The study offers an objective measure of how noisy the streets are.
examples.cn: 这项研究提供了街道噪声程度的客观量度。

examples.en: Our objective for the year is to reduce waste by a third.
examples.cn: 我们今年的目标是把浪费减少三分之一。

examples.en: He tried to stay objective, but the photographs made him angry.
examples.cn: 他努力保持客观，但那些照片让他愤怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊不，接个物体」——先别急着评判，把摆在面前的物体接住看清楚 → objective 客观的、目标

root: 拉丁语 objectum“被摆到面前的东西”= ob“在前”+ iacere“投、掷”，加 -ive；objective 字面“与摆在面前的对象相关的”，由“客体”引出“客观”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of objective all turn on one act: throwing something in front. First it is an object of thought, then a real thing outside, then an impartial view, then a target on a map.
sensesIntro.cn: objective 的九个义项都围绕一个动作：把某物投到前方。它先是思想的对象，再是心外的实物，再是不偏不倚的看法，最后成为地图上的靶点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed in front of the mind or the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件被摆到心智或视线之前的东西。

branches.en: THE OBJECT IN THE MIND: the 1610s philosophical sense, where the object is still a thought.
branches.cn: 心中的对象：17 世纪初的哲学义，对象仍是一种思想。

branches.en: REALITY AND EVIDENCE: the object outside the mind, and the facts that can be checked.
branches.cn: 现实与证据：心外的对象，以及可以核查的事实。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINED OBSERVER: impartial judgment, and description without interpretation.
branches.cn: 受约束的观察者：不偏不倚的判断，以及不带解释的描述。

branches.en: THE AIM: a military point to be taken, and the general goal that grew from it.
branches.cn: 目标：要夺取的军事据点，以及由此长出的普通目的。

branches.en: TECHNICAL OBJECTS: the lens facing the object, and the grammatical object case.
branches.cn: 技术性对象：朝向物体的镜片，以及语法中的宾格。

intro.en: Objective is the Latin adjective objectivus in English form: object- plus -ive. The root sits in ob- 'before' and iacere 'to throw', the same root that gives subject, adjective and object.
intro.cn: objective 是拉丁形容词 objectivus 的英语形式：object- 加 -ive。词根在 ob-“在前”与 iacere“投”里，也是 subject、adjective、object 的共同来源。

latinIntro.en: Latin objectum 'thing put before' is the neuter noun from obicere; objectivus was used by Duns Scotus. The same iacere also builds subjectum 'thrown under' and adiectivus 'thrown to'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 objectum“被摆到前面之物”是 obicere 的中性名词；objectivus 由邓斯·司各脱使用。同一个 iacere 还构成 subjectum“投在下面”和 adiectivus“投向”。

items.meaning: relating to the object; impartial; a goal
items.meaningCN: 与对象相关的；客观的；目标（-ive 构成形容词，也可作名词）
items.example: The review aims to be objective.
items.exampleCN: 这篇评论力求客观。

items.meaning: in an impartial, fact-based way
items.meaningCN: 客观地；不带偏见地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The team judged the design objectively.
items.exampleCN: 团队客观地评估了这项设计。

items.meaning: the quality of being objective
items.meaningCN: 客观性；无偏见（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: Journalists are expected to maintain objectivity.
items.exampleCN: 记者应当保持客观。

items.meaning: a thing put before the senses; to oppose
items.meaningCN: 物体；对象；反对（ob-“在前”+ iect“投”）
items.example: A strange object lay on the path.
items.exampleCN: 小路上躺着一个奇怪的物体。

items.meaning: a statement thrown against something; disagreement
items.meaningCN: 异议；反对（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The lawyer raised an objection.
items.exampleCN: 律师提出了异议。

items.meaning: to treat as an object or make concrete
items.meaningCN: 使物化；使具体化（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: The advertisement objectifies the people it shows.
items.exampleCN: 这则广告把画面中的人物化了。

items.meaning: the act of treating someone as an object
items.meaningCN: 物化；对象化（-ication 构成名词）
items.example: The essay discusses the objectification of labour.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章讨论劳动的物化。

items.meaning: literally 'thrown to'; a word added to a noun
items.meaningCN: 字面“投向”；形容词（加在名词上的词）
items.example: Choose a precise adjective for the noun.
items.exampleCN: 为这个名词选一个准确的形容词。

items.meaning: literally 'thrown under'; a topic or a grammatical subject
items.meaningCN: 字面“投在下面”；主题；主语
items.example: The subject of the talk was water.
items.exampleCN: 讲座的主题是水。

items.meaning: based on personal feeling rather than the object
items.meaningCN: 主观的（subject + -ive，从“主体”出发）
items.example: Taste in music is subjective.
items.exampleCN: 音乐品味是主观的。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to an object; existing as an object of thought
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与对象相关的；作为思想对象存在的（邓斯·司各脱用语）

definition_zh: 获得；得到；取得；赢得；（古）握有；（规则、习俗）通行
definition_en: to get or acquire something, especially through effort, request, or established right
core_image: 伸手向前，抓住一件东西并握牢
scene: A researcher waits at a government office window for two hours to obtain a signed permit.
sceneCN: 这里 obtain 是「取得、拿到」（第 2 个义项：通过努力或申请得到）；句意：研究人员在政府办事窗口等了两个小时，才取得一份签好字的许可证。图中可辨识物件：许可证、办事窗口、印章、签字笔、排号单。

pos.zh: 获得；取得；赢得
（规则、习俗等）通行；存在

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: Take Hold: come to have something
senses.titleCN: 抓住：使某物归自己所有
senses.definition: to get or acquire something so that it becomes yours
senses.definitionCN: 得到或取得某物，使之归自己所有
senses.example: She obtained a copy of the report from the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 她从档案馆取得了一份报告副本。
senses.why: Latin obtinere joined ob- 'in front of' to tenere 'to hold'. The first sense is physical: you reach forward and close your hand on something, so obtain means to get it into your possession.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obtinere 把 ob-“在前”加在 tenere“握持”上。第一个义项是身体性的：你向前伸手，把东西握在手里，于是 obtain 意为“使某物进入自己的占有”。

senses.title: Earn the Hold: secure through effort
senses.titleCN: 挣得握持：通过努力取得
senses.definition: to succeed in getting something after effort, application, or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力、申请或协商后成功得到某物
senses.example: It took three meetings to obtain the funding.
senses.exampleCN: 取得这笔资金开了三次会。
senses.why: A grip that must be worked for is still a grip. The hand reaches farther and closes later, so obtain adds the idea of effort to plain getting.
senses.whyCN: 需要费力才得到的握持仍然是握持。手伸得更远、合拢得更晚，于是 obtain 在“得到”之上加了“付出努力”的意思。

senses.title: Come By It: inherit or receive
senses.titleCN: 得自他人：继承或受赠
senses.definition: in older use, to come into possession of something by inheritance or by receiving it
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指通过继承或受赠而占有某物
senses.example: He obtained the land from his father.
senses.exampleCN: 他从父亲那里继承了这块土地。
senses.why: The early French and Latin record lists 'inherit' among the senses of obtain. The thing still passes into your hold, but the reaching is done by family or gift rather than by effort.
senses.whyCN: 早期法语和拉丁语记录把“继承”列为 obtain 的义项之一。东西仍然进入你的握持，但伸手的是家族或赠予，而不是努力。

senses.title: Win the Field: obtain a victory
senses.titleCN: 夺得战场：赢得胜利
senses.definition: to gain or win something such as a victory, advantage, or right, often against opposition
senses.definitionCN: 赢得胜利、优势或权利等，常指对抗之中取得
senses.example: The small force obtained a decisive victory at the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这支小部队在隘口取得了决定性胜利。
senses.why: Early records also give 'conquer' as a sense. To obtain a victory is to take hold of the outcome after struggle, the same grip won against someone else.
senses.whyCN: 早期记录还给出“征服”义。obtain a victory 就是在争斗之后握住结果，是同一只从对手那里赢来的手。

senses.title: Hold Fast: the archaic sense of possession
senses.titleCN: 握牢不放：古老的占有义
senses.definition: in archaic use, to hold, keep, or possess something rather than to get it
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法，指握持、保留或占有某物，而不是“得到”
senses.example: The old charter says the family shall obtain the manor for a thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 那份古老契据说，该家族应握有这座庄园一千年。
senses.why: Obtinere in Latin could mean 'hold fast' as well as 'get possession of'. English kept the holding sense for a while: the hand is already closed and stays closed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obtinere 既可指“握牢”，也可指“取得占有”。英语一度保留了“握持”义：手已经合拢，并且一直不松开。

senses.title: The Custom Obtains: be current in practice
senses.titleCN: 习俗通行：在实际中成立
senses.definition: to be prevalent or customary, to be established in practice, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 盛行或成为惯例，在实际中确立，作不及物动词
senses.example: The custom still obtains in the mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在山村里仍然通行。
senses.why: From the 1610s the intransitive sense appears. A practice that 'holds' among people is one that grips the community, so obtain comes to mean 'be current'.
senses.whyCN: 不及物义自 17 世纪 10 年代出现。一种做法在人群中“握得住”，就是抓住了整个社群，于是 obtain 意为“通行、成立”。

senses.title: Obtain Permission: the formal request
senses.titleCN: 获得许可：正式申请
senses.definition: to succeed in getting official permission, consent, or approval through the proper channel
senses.definitionCN: 通过正当渠道成功取得官方许可、同意或批准
senses.example: You must obtain written consent before using the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 使用这些照片前必须取得书面同意。
senses.why: Here the grip is granted by an authority. You put a request forward, the office puts a signed paper forward, and the paper passes into your hand.
senses.whyCN: 这里的握持由权力机构授予。你把申请递到前面，办事窗口把签好的文件递到前面，文件最终进入你的手中。

senses.title: Obtain Data: gather what is out there
senses.titleCN: 获取数据：把在外面的东西取回
senses.definition: to get information, measurements, or evidence, often by going to the source
senses.definitionCN: 取得信息、测量值或证据，常指到源头去取
senses.example: The team obtained samples from twelve different sites.
senses.exampleCN: 团队从十二个不同地点取得了样本。
senses.why: Data exist outside you and must be brought into reach. The old forward reach fits research: you go to the source, take the reading, and hold it as a record.
senses.whyCN: 数据存在于你之外，必须被带进可及范围。古老的“向前伸手”正适合研究：你到源头去，取回读数，并把它作为记录握在手里。

senses.title: Obtain a Degree: earn a standing
senses.titleCN: 取得学位：挣得一种资格
senses.definition: to complete the requirements for and receive a qualification, degree, or position
senses.definitionCN: 完成要求并取得资格、学位或职位
senses.example: She obtained her doctorate after six years of research.
senses.exampleCN: 经过六年研究，她取得了博士学位。
senses.why: A degree is conferred after requirements are met, yet it still enters your hold. The thing obtained here is a standing you can keep and carry.
senses.whyCN: 学位是在满足要求后授予的，但它仍然进入你的握持。这里取得的东西是一种你可以保有并带走的身份资格。

intro.en: Obtain entered English in the early 15th century from Old French obtenir or directly from Latin obtinere 'hold fast, get possession of'. The holding image in tenere is the core, and the intransitive 'be prevalent' sense followed in the 1610s.
intro.cn: obtain 于 15 世纪初从古法语 obtenir 或直接拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”进入英语。tenere 的“握持”意象是核心，不及物的“通行”义则于 17 世纪 10 年代出现。

items.en: Recorded as obteinen, meaning 'to get or acquire, inherit, gain, conquer'.
items.cn: 以 obteinen 形式记录，意为“得到或取得、继承、获得、征服”。

items.en: From Old French obtenir (14c.) or directly from Latin obtinere 'hold, hold fast, take hold of, get possession of, acquire'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 obtenir（14 世纪），或直接来自拉丁语 obtinere“握持、握牢、抓住、取得占有、获得”。

items.en: Obtinere is ob- 'in front of' (here possibly intensive) plus tenere 'to hold'.
items.cn: obtinere 是 ob-“在前”（此处也可能是强调用法）加 tenere“握持”。

items.en: Tenere is generally traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch', the same root family as tenant and tenacity.
items.cn: tenere 一般认为可追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”，与 tenant、tenacity 同属一个词根家族。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'be prevalent or customary, be established in practice' is recorded.
items.cn: 记录到不及物义“盛行或成为惯例、在实际中确立”。

items.en: The verb yields obtainable, unobtainable, obtainment and obtainer. Its ob- prefix is shared with occupy (ob- + capere 'seize') and occur (ob- + currere 'run'), but the roots differ.
items.cn: 这个动词派生出 obtainable、unobtainable、obtainment、obtainer。它的 ob- 前缀与 occupy（ob- + capere“抓取”）、occur（ob- + currere“跑”）相同，但词根不同。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the -tain ending; the near-meaning group holds words that approach 'get' from different angles.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 -tain 结尾；近义组是从不同角度接近“得到”的词。

entries.definition: to hold inside. It shares tenere 'to hold' with obtain, but con- means 'together', so the holding is inward.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳；包含。它与 obtain 共用 tenere“握持”，但 con- 意为“一起”，握持方向朝内。

entries.definition: to keep or continue to hold. The re- prefix points back, so the grip stays rather than being newly acquired.
entries.definitionCN: 保留；继续握有。前缀 re- 指向回，握持是留在手里，而不是新取得。

entries.definition: to reach or achieve. It looks like obtain but comes from ad- plus tangere 'to touch', not from tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 达到；获得。它看起来像 obtain，但来自 ad- 加 tangere“触摸”，不是 tenere。

entries.definition: to get or come to possess something, often over time. It is more formal than obtain and stresses the process.
entries.definitionCN: 取得；逐渐占有。它比 obtain 更正式，更强调过程。

entries.definition: to get something useful or advantageous. It often implies an increase, while obtain is neutral about value.
entries.definitionCN: 获得（有用或有利的东西）。它常含“增加”，obtain 对价值是中性的。

entries.definition: to get something after effort and make it safe to keep. It adds certainty to the plain act of obtaining.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力取得并确保保住。它在“得到”之上加了“确保”。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: ob- plus tenere 'to hold', the -tain family of contain, retain and sustain, and the fixed phrase 'the custom obtains'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：ob- 加 tenere“握持”、contain／retain／sustain 的 -tain 词族，以及固定说法 the custom obtains。

normal.en: Ob- 'in front of' plus tenere 'to hold' makes obtain: to get a hold of something.
normal.cn: ob-“在前”加 tenere“握持”构成 obtain：抓住某物、取得握持。

normal.en: Contain, retain and sustain all share tenere; only the prefix tells you which direction the holding goes.
normal.cn: contain、retain、sustain 都共用 tenere；只有前缀告诉你握持的方向。

normal.en: Obtain, occupy and occur share ob-, but their roots differ: tenere 'hold', capere 'seize', currere 'run'.
normal.cn: obtain、occupy、occur 共用 ob-，但词根不同：tenere“握”、capere“抓”、currere“跑”。

normal.en: Obtain permission is the standard formal frame for an official yes.
normal.cn: obtain permission 是取得官方许可的标准正式搭配。

normal.en: The custom obtains is the intransitive survivor: a practice holds among people.
normal.cn: the custom obtains 是不及物义的存留：一种做法在人群中握得住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching forward and closing around a handle; the handle is now yours to keep.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手向前伸出，握住一个把手；这个把手现在归你保有。

abstract.en: The same grip can be laid on a custom: a practice holds a whole community in place.
abstract.cn: 同一只握持的手可以放在习俗上：一种做法把整个社群握在原地。

abstract.en: At a counter, a signed paper slides forward into your hand: obtaining is that moment of transfer.
abstract.cn: 在办事窗口，一份签好的文件滑向前方、进入你手中：obtain 就是交接的那一刻。

examples.en: The laboratory obtained the samples from three rivers in the region.
examples.cn: 实验室从该地区的三条河流取得了样本。

examples.en: Students must obtain permission before filming inside the museum.
examples.cn: 学生在博物馆内拍摄前必须获得许可。

examples.en: That rule no longer obtains in most modern cities.
examples.cn: 那条规则在大多数现代城市已不再通行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额不，抬恩」——伸手一抬，把恩赐的东西接住 → obtain 获得、取得

root: 拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”= ob“在前”+ tenere“握持”（一般认为追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of obtain all keep one gesture: a hand reaches forward and closes. It can close on an object, a victory, a permission, a set of data, a degree, or even a custom that holds a community.
sensesIntro.cn: obtain 的九个义项都保留同一个动作：手向前伸出并合拢。它握住的可以是物件、胜利、许可、数据、学位，甚至一种握住了社群的习俗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching forward and closing on something.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手向前伸出，把某物握在掌中。

branches.en: COMING TO HAVE: acquiring something, and receiving it by inheritance.
branches.cn: 归于己有：取得某物，以及通过继承得到。

branches.en: CONTESTED GAINS: securing something by effort, and winning a victory.
branches.cn: 争夺而得：靠努力取得，以及赢得胜利。

branches.en: HOLDING FAST: the archaic sense of keeping what is already in hand.
branches.cn: 握牢不放：保留手中已有之物的古义。

branches.en: HOLDING AMONG PEOPLE: a custom or rule that obtains, still current.
branches.cn: 在人群中成立：仍然通行的习俗或规则。

branches.en: FORMAL ACQUISITION: permission, data, and a qualification all pass into your hold.
branches.cn: 正式取得：许可、数据和学位资格都进入你的握持。

intro.en: Obtain is ob- plus the Latin root tenere 'to hold'. English adds -able, -ment and -er, while the same -tain root appears in contain, retain, sustain, tenant and maintain.
intro.cn: obtain 是 ob- 加拉丁词根 tenere“握持”。英语加 -able、-ment、-er，而同一个 -tain 词根出现在 contain、retain、sustain、tenant、maintain 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin obtinere 'hold fast, get possession' is ob- plus tenere 'to hold'. Tenere is generally traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch'; it is not related to capere 'seize' or currere 'run', which build occupy and occur.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”是 ob- 加 tenere“握持”。tenere 一般认为追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”；它与 capere“抓取”、currere“跑”无关，后两者构成 occupy 和 occur。

items.meaning: to get a hold of; to acquire
items.meaningCN: 抓住；获得（ob-“在前”+ tenere“握持”）
items.example: They obtained the land through a legal purchase.
items.exampleCN: 他们通过合法购买取得了这片土地。

items.meaning: possible to obtain
items.meaningCN: 可获得的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: The tickets are obtainable only at the door.
items.exampleCN: 票只能在门口买到。

items.meaning: impossible to obtain
items.meaningCN: 无法获得的（un-“不”+ obtainable）
items.example: The rare mineral is almost unobtainable now.
items.exampleCN: 这种稀有矿物如今几乎无法获得。

items.meaning: the act of obtaining
items.meaningCN: 获得；取得（-ment 构成动作名词）
items.example: The obtainment of a visa took several weeks.
items.exampleCN: 取得签证花了数周。

items.meaning: a person who obtains something
items.meaningCN: 获得者；取得者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The first obtainer of the map was a naval officer.
items.exampleCN: 第一个得到这张地图的人是一名海军军官。

items.meaning: to hold inside
items.meaningCN: 容纳；包含（con-“一起”+ tenere“握持”）
items.example: The box contains old letters.
items.exampleCN: 盒子里装着旧信件。

items.meaning: to keep or continue to hold
items.meaningCN: 保留；继续握有（re-“回”+ tenere）
items.example: The soil retains water after rain.
items.exampleCN: 雨后土壤能保住水分。

items.structure: sus- (sub-, from below) + tain (tenere, to hold)
items.meaning: to hold up or keep going
items.meaningCN: 支撑；维持（sus- 即 sub-“在下”+ tenere）
items.example: The beams sustain the weight of the roof.
items.exampleCN: 这些梁支撑着屋顶的重量。

items.meaning: a person who holds a lease
items.meaningCN: 租户；房客（ten-“握持”+ -ant 表示人）
items.example: The tenant pays rent on the first day of the month.
items.exampleCN: 租户在每月第一天交房租。

items.meaning: to keep in good condition; to hold a view
items.meaningCN: 维持；保养；坚持（manu“手”+ tenere“握持”）
items.example: The crew maintains the bridge every summer.
items.exampleCN: 养路队每年夏天维护这座桥。

latinEntries.meaning: hold, hold fast, take hold of, get possession of, acquire
latinEntries.meaningCN: 握持；握牢；抓住；取得占有；获得
握；持；抓住（一般认为追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”）

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；一目了然的；显眼的；（古义）常见的
definition_en: so clear or easy to see that it needs no explanation; standing openly in view
core_image: 一块石头正挡在必经之路中央，迎面撞上，想不看都难
scene: The crack in the dam was obvious even from the far bank.
sceneCN: 这里 obvious 是「一眼可见、无法忽略」（第 2 个义项：显而易见）；句意：即使从对岸看，堤坝上的裂缝也一目了然。图中可辨识物件：坝体上的裂缝、渗出的水流、对岸的观察者、手中的望远镜。

pos.zh: 明显的；显而易见的；一目了然的

collocations.zh: 说人人都知道的事；多此一举地明说

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: In the way: the Latin core sense
senses.titleCN: 挡在路上：拉丁语的本义
senses.definition: in the literal Latin sense, placed directly in someone's path so as to meet them face to face
senses.definitionCN: 按拉丁语本义，指正处在某人前行的路上，与对方迎面相遇
senses.example: In Latin, an obvius thing was one that lay in your way and met you head-on.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语里，obvius 的东西就是横在你路上、与你迎面相遇的东西。
senses.why: Latin obvius came from obviam, 'in the way': ob 'in front of, against' plus viam, the accusative of via 'way'. The first picture is a physical obstacle standing in the road.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obvius 出自 obviam“在路上”：ob“在前、迎着”加 viam（via“路”的宾格）。最初的画面就是一件挡在路中的实体障碍。

senses.title: Plain to see: impossible to miss
senses.titleCN: 显而易见：想错过都难
senses.definition: visible at once, without searching and without being told
senses.definitionCN: 一眼就能看见，既不用寻找，也不用别人告知
senses.example: The crack in the dam was obvious even from the far bank.
senses.exampleCN: 即使从对岸看，坝体上的裂缝也一目了然。
senses.why: Something standing in the road meets the eye before the mind has time to search for it. This is the 'plain to see' sense recorded from the 1630s.
senses.whyCN: 挡在路上的东西会在脑子来得及寻找之前先撞进眼睛，这就是 17 世纪 30 年代记录下来的“显而易见”义。

senses.title: Easy to understand: no explanation needed
senses.titleCN: 容易理解：不必解释
senses.definition: so clear that the mind grasps it immediately, without a chain of reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到脑子立刻就能抓住，不需要一连串推理
senses.example: The rule was obvious once the teacher gave a single example.
senses.exampleCN: 老师只举了一个例子，这条规则就变得明明白白。
senses.why: The road here is the road of thought: an idea that lies across the mind's path is reached without a detour, so understanding feels immediate.
senses.whyCN: 这里的路是思维之路：横在思路上的想法不必绕道就能抵达，于是理解显得毫不费力。

senses.title: Open and unconcealed: not hidden
senses.titleCN: 公开不藏：无从遮掩
senses.definition: not concealed or disguised; showing plainly what is actually there
senses.definitionCN: 没有隐藏或伪装，把实际存在的东西直接显露出来
senses.example: His disappointment was obvious to everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌边每个人都看得出他的失望。
senses.why: Latin obvius also meant 'open, exposed'. What is exposed is literally placed in front of the eyes, so there is nothing left to hide behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obvius 还兼有“敞开、暴露”的意思。被暴露的东西就摆在眼前，已经没有可以遮挡的余地。

senses.title: The obvious choice: what anyone would pick
senses.titleCN: 不二之选：谁都会挑的那个
senses.definition: the answer or option so natural that no other seems worth considering
senses.definitionCN: 自然到让人觉得别的选项都不值一提的答案或选择
senses.example: For a first bicycle, the obvious choice is a small, cheap one.
senses.exampleCN: 第一辆自行车，明摆着的选择是买一辆小而便宜的。
senses.why: When only one option stands in the road ahead, it looks like the only road there is; what is plainly visible becomes what is expected.
senses.whyCN: 当前方路上只立着一个选项，它看起来就是唯一的路；看得见的东西于是变成了理所当然的东西。

senses.title: Barefaced: an obvious lie or mistake
senses.titleCN: 赤裸裸：明摆着的谎言或错误
senses.definition: used of faults so plain that no one could pretend not to see them
senses.definitionCN: 用于明显到谁也无法假装看不见的过失
senses.example: The excuse was an obvious lie, and nobody at the meeting believed it.
senses.exampleCN: 那个借口是赤裸裸的谎言，会上没人相信。
senses.why: A falsehood that stands in plain sight is shameless: the visibility itself becomes the accusation, so obvious adds contempt in this use.
senses.whyCN: 摆在明处的假话是无耻的：可见性本身成了指控，因此这一用法里的 obvious 带上了轻蔑。

senses.title: Obsolete: frequently met with, commonplace
senses.titleCN: 古义：常见的、司空见惯的
senses.definition: the earliest recorded sense, 'often encountered, ordinary', now no longer in use
senses.definitionCN: 最早记录的义项“经常遇到、平常”，今已不再使用
senses.example: Early writers used obvious for a sight so common that it drew no comment.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作家用 obvious 形容常见到无人置评的景象。
senses.why: A thing met again and again on the road stops being noticed at all. The 1580s sense was 'frequently met with', and modern English dropped that branch.
senses.whyCN: 在路上反复遇到的东西会彻底失去存在感。16 世纪 80 年代的义项正是“常常遇到”，现代英语丢掉了这条分支。

senses.title: Self-evident: true without proof
senses.titleCN: 不证自明：无需论证即成立
senses.definition: true in a way that needs no argument or evidence to support it
senses.definitionCN: 真实到不需要论证或证据来支撑
senses.example: The declaration calls these truths self-evident rather than proven.
senses.exampleCN: 宣言称这些真理不证自明，而不是被证明的。
senses.why: If a fact blocks the path of doubt, no proof is needed to get around it; the road metaphor turns logical and becomes self-evidence.
senses.whyCN: 如果事实挡住了怀疑的路，就不需要证据绕行；路的比喻转为逻辑意义，成为“不证自明”。

senses.title: The obvious: a noun phrase
senses.titleCN: 显而易见的事：名词性用法
senses.definition: used as a noun in phrases such as state the obvious, meaning what everyone already knows
senses.definitionCN: 用于 state the obvious 一类短语，指人人都已知道的事
senses.example: He kept stating the obvious: that the road ahead was flooded.
senses.exampleCN: 他不停地说显而易见的事：前面的路被淹了。
senses.why: English lets an adjective stand for the thing it describes. The obvious is whatever is visible to all, and saying it aloud is the fixed phrase state the obvious.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许形容词代替它所描述的事物。the obvious 就是所有人都看得见的东西，把它说出来便成了固定短语 state the obvious。

intro.en: Obvious entered English in the 1580s from Latin obvius, literally 'in the way'. The meaning 'plain to see' is recorded from the 1630s, and the old 'commonplace' sense has died out.
intro.cn: obvious 于 16 世纪 80 年代从拉丁语 obvius 进入英语，字面是“在路上的”。“显而易见”义自 17 世纪 30 年代有记录，而旧的“司空见惯”义已消亡。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'frequently met with, commonplace', a meaning that has since become obsolete.
items.cn: 最早记录的义项是“经常遇到、平常”，此义后来废弃。

items.en: From Latin obvius 'that is in the way, presenting itself readily, open, exposed, commonplace'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 obvius“挡在路上的、自己送上门的、敞开的、暴露的、平常的”。

items.en: Obvius goes back to the adverb obviam 'in the way', built on ob 'in front of, against' plus viam, the accusative of via 'way'.
items.cn: obvius 出自副词 obviam“在路上”，由 ob“在前、迎着”加 viam（via“路”的宾格）构成。

items.en: Ob continues PIE *epi / *opi 'near, against'; via continues PIE *wegh- 'to go, move', the same root that gives way and wagon.
items.cn: ob 追溯到原始印欧语 *epi / *opi“近、对着”；via 追溯到 *wegh-“走、移动”，way 与 wagon 同出这个词根。

items.en: 'Plain to see, evident' is recorded from the 1630s, and this is the sense that modern English kept.
items.cn: “显而易见、明白”自 17 世纪 30 年代有记录，这正是现代英语保留的义项。

items.en: The visible branch survives in obvious, obviously and obviousness; the physical 'in the way' image survives separately in obviate and in the prefix ob-.
items.cn: “可见”这一支保留在 obvious、obviously、obviousness 中；物理性的“挡在路上”意象则另存于 obviate 和前缀 ob- 里。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to remove a difficulty or need in advance. It shares ob plus via 'way' and keeps the literal 'clear the road' image.
entries.definitionCN: 提前消除困难或需要。它同出 ob + via“路”，保留了字面的“清路”意象。

entries.definition: unaware of something happening around one. It looks close but comes from Latin oblivio 'forgetfulness', not from via.
entries.definitionCN: 对周围发生的事毫无察觉。它形似 obvious，却来自拉丁语 oblivio“遗忘”，与 via 无关。

entries.definition: feeling envy. It shares the -vious ending but goes back to Latin invidia 'envy', not to obvius.
entries.definitionCN: 嫉妒的。它同样以 -vious 结尾，但词源是拉丁语 invidia“嫉妒”，并非 obvius。

entries.definition: clear from the evidence available. It is more formal and often points to proof, while obvious points to the thing meeting the eye.
entries.definitionCN: 从已有证据看很清楚。它更正式，常指向证据；obvious 则强调事物自己撞进眼里。

entries.definition: seeming true from what is seen, which may or may not be the case. Obvious carries no such doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 从所见看来像是真的，但未必如此。obvious 不含有这层怀疑。

entries.definition: easy to see, hear or understand. It is broader and can describe sound and writing as well as sight.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见、听见或理解。它范围更广，除视觉外也能形容声音和文字。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin parts ob plus via, the via family in deviate and previous, and the fixed phrase state the obvious.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + via，deviate 与 previous 中的 via 词族，以及固定短语 state the obvious。

normal.en: ob 'in front of' plus via 'way' gives 'in the way': the thing is standing in your road, so it meets you face to face.
normal.cn: ob“在前”加 via“路”就是“在路中”：东西挡在你的路上，于是与你迎面相遇。

normal.en: via, deviate, previous and trivial all contain via 'way'; obvious is the member of the family that stands in the way.
normal.cn: via、deviate、previous、trivial 都含 via“路”；obvious 是这个词族里“挡在路上”的那一个。

normal.en: The oldest sense was 'commonplace': something met on the road every day stops being noticed.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是“司空见惯”：天天在路上遇到的东西，反而不再被注意。

normal.en: State the obvious is a fixed phrase for saying what everyone can already see.
normal.cn: state the obvious 是固定短语，指把人人早已看见的事再说一遍。

normal.en: Obviously and obviousness are the everyday adverb and noun built on the same adjective.
normal.cn: obviously 和 obviousness 是由同一个形容词构成的日常副词和名词。

abstract.en: Picture a road with one boulder in the middle: you do not go looking for it, it comes to you.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路中央横着一块巨石：不是你去寻找它，而是它迎着你来。

abstract.en: The same boulder can lie on the road of thought, so a fact, a lie or a choice can all be 'in the way'.
abstract.cn: 同一块石头也能横在思维之路上，所以一个事实、一句谎话或一个选择都可以“挡在路上”。

abstract.en: When nothing blocks the road, understanding is instant; when everything is on the road, the word slides into 'commonplace'.
abstract.cn: 路上没有阻挡时，理解是瞬间的；路上全是东西时，这个词就滑向“司空见惯”。

examples.en: It was obvious from the empty shelves that the storm had caused panic buying.
examples.cn: 从空荡荡的货架一眼就能看出，风暴引发了抢购。

examples.en: She made the obvious mistake of trusting a stranger with her luggage.
examples.cn: 她犯了一个明显的错误，把行李交给了陌生人。

examples.en: The solution looks obvious only after someone has pointed it out.
examples.cn: 解决方案只有在别人指出来之后才显得显而易见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，不喂我死」——哦，不喂我就要死，这么明显的事还用说 → obvious 明显的、显而易见的

root: 源自拉丁语 obvius“挡在路上的、迎面而来的”= ob“在前、迎着”+ via“路”，核心是“横在路上、一眼撞见”；更深的 *epi / *wegh- 为原始印欧语构拟。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of obvious all start from one picture: a stone standing in the middle of the road. The same obstacle then moves from the eye to the mind, to expectation, to shamelessness, and finally back to the oldest sense of 'commonplace'.
sensesIntro.cn: obvious 的九个义项都从同一幅画出发：一块石头立在路中央。同一个障碍随后从眼睛走到思维，走到理所当然，走到无耻，最后又回到最古老的“司空见惯”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone standing in the middle of the road, meeting you head-on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头立在路中央，迎面与你相遇。

branches.en: THE LITERAL OBSTACLE: the Latin thing that lies in the road and comes toward you.
branches.cn: 字面的障碍：拉丁语中横在路上、朝你而来的东西。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE: what stands in the open is seen at once and cannot be hidden.
branches.cn: 可见之物：摆在明处的东西一眼可见，也无从隐藏。

branches.en: THE CLEAR IDEA: the obstacle moves onto the road of thought, so understanding needs no detour or proof.
branches.cn: 清晰的想法：障碍移到思维之路上，理解不必绕道，也不必证明。

branches.en: THE ONLY OPTION AND THE BAREFACED: what is plainly visible becomes expected, and a visible fault becomes shameless.
branches.cn: 唯一选项与赤裸裸：看得见的东西变成理所当然，看得见的过失变成无耻。

branches.en: THE COMMONPLACE: what is met every day stops being noticed, and the adjective becomes the noun in the obvious.
branches.cn: 司空见惯：天天遇到的东西不再被注意；形容词也在 the obvious 中变成名词。

intro.en: Obvious is Latin ob- 'in front of, against' plus via 'way', with the adjective suffix -ous. English then adds -ly, -ness and the negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: obvious 由拉丁语 ob-“在前、迎着”加 via“路”，再加形容词后缀 -ous 构成。英语随后又加 -ly、-ness 和否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin obvius, from obviam 'in the way'; via 'way' is the noun at its centre.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 obvius，出自 obviam“在路上”；位于中心的正是名词 via“路”。

items.meaning: standing in the way, therefore plain to see
items.meaningCN: 挡在路上因而显而易见的（-ous 构成形容词）
items.example: The answer was obvious to the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 全班都觉得答案显而易见。

items.meaning: plainly; in a way that needs no explanation
items.meaningCN: 明显地；显然（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Obviously, the bridge is too narrow for trucks.
items.exampleCN: 显然，这座桥对卡车来说太窄了。

items.meaning: the quality of being easy to see or understand
items.meaningCN: 明显；显而易见（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: The obviousness of the error embarrassed the editor.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误如此明显，让编辑很尴尬。

items.meaning: not immediately visible or easy to understand
items.meaningCN: 不明显的；不易看出的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The link between the two events is unobvious but real.
items.exampleCN: 两件事之间的联系并不明显，但确实存在。

items.meaning: to clear a difficulty out of the way
items.meaningCN: 消除；排除（障碍）
items.example: A second entrance would obviate the need for queues.
items.exampleCN: 再开一个入口就不必排队了。

items.meaning: the act of removing a need or difficulty
items.meaningCN: 排除；预防（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The obviation of the old permit saved weeks of work.
items.exampleCN: 取消旧许可证省下了好几周的工作。

items.meaning: to move away from the road or the standard
items.meaningCN: 偏离；脱离（离开原来的路）
items.example: The pilot had to deviate from the planned route.
items.exampleCN: 飞行员不得不偏离原定航线。

items.meaning: a departure from a route or standard
items.meaningCN: 偏离；偏差
items.example: Any deviation from the recipe changes the taste.
items.exampleCN: 任何偏离食谱的做法都会改变味道。

items.meaning: going before on the way; earlier
items.meaningCN: 先行的；以前的（pre-“在前”+ via“路”）
items.example: The previous owner kept the keys in the shed.
items.exampleCN: 前一任房主把钥匙放在棚子里。

items.meaning: belonging to the crossroads, hence common and unimportant
items.meaningCN: 十字路口的，因而平常、不重要的
items.example: They argued over trivial details for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们为一个琐碎细节争论了一个小时。

latinEntries.meaning: in the way, open, exposed, commonplace
latinEntries.meaningCN: 挡在路上的；敞开的；暴露的；平常的

latinEntries.structure: via (noun, ablative viā also used as preposition)

latinEntries.meaning: to meet, to go against, to prevent

definition_zh: 占据；占用；占领；居住在；担任；使忙碌
definition_en: to take and hold something — a place, a space, a period of time, a post, or a person's attention
core_image: 一只手压住并攥紧一件东西，占住不放
scene: Boxes occupy most of the attic and leave only a narrow path to the window.
sceneCN: 这里 occupy 是「占去空间」（第 2 个义项：占据空间）；句意：箱子占去阁楼的大部分空间，只留下一条通往窗户的窄道。图中可辨识物件：成堆的纸箱、阁楼的横梁、窄窄的走道、窗子。

pos.zh: 占据；占用；占领；担任；使忙于

collocations.zh: 担任某职位；占据某位置

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

derivatives.zh: 心事重重的；专注的（pre-“预先”+ occupy）

senses.title: Seize and hold: take possession
senses.titleCN: 抓住不放：取得占有
senses.definition: to take possession of a place or thing and keep control of it
senses.definitionCN: 取得对某地或某物的占有，并保持控制
senses.example: The troops occupied the fort before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 部队在黎明前占领了要塞。
senses.why: Latin occupare was an emphatic form of ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp, seize'. The core picture is a hand closing over something and not letting go.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occupare 是 ob“覆在……之上”加 capere“抓、夺”的强调形式。核心画面就是一只手合拢抓住东西，不再放开。

senses.title: Take up space: fill a surface
senses.titleCN: 占去空间：铺满一块地方
senses.definition: to fill or cover an area of space, so that little room is left
senses.definitionCN: 填满或覆盖一块空间，几乎不留余地
senses.example: The piano occupies one corner of the living room.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴占了客厅的一个角落。
senses.why: A thing that holds a place holds it in the same grip: the floor under it is no longer free. Possession becomes measurement of space.
senses.whyCN: 占住一个位置的东西用的是同一个“握”：它下面的地板不再空着。占有于是变成对空间的度量。

senses.title: Take up time: fill a period
senses.titleCN: 占去时间：填满一段时间
senses.definition: to use up a period of time, leaving it unavailable for anything else
senses.definitionCN: 用掉一段时间，使其无法再做别的事
senses.example: The hearing occupied the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 听证会占了整整一个下午。
senses.why: Hours can be held just as floors can: once a period is gripped by an activity, it cannot be handed to another.
senses.whyCN: 小时和地板一样可以被“握住”：一段时间一旦被某项活动抓住，就无法再交给别的活动。

senses.title: Live in: hold as a home
senses.titleCN: 居住：把某处当作住所
senses.definition: to live in or use a building as one's home or base
senses.definitionCN: 住在某处，或以某建筑为住所、驻地
senses.example: The family occupies the upper floors of the building.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人住在楼的上层。
senses.why: Living somewhere is holding it continuously. The legal phrase 'occupier' grew from exactly this: the person who is in possession of the property.
senses.whyCN: 住在某处就是持续地占住它。法律用语 occupier 正由此而来：实际占有该房产的人。

senses.title: Hold an office, post or rank
senses.titleCN: 担任职位：占住一个位置
senses.definition: to hold a job, office or official position
senses.definitionCN: 担任某项工作、职务或正式职位
senses.example: She occupies the chair of the department.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任系主任一职。
senses.why: A post is a place in an institution; whoever holds it fills that slot. The space sense turns social: the seat is taken by a person.
senses.whyCN: 职位是机构里的一个位置，谁担任就由谁填进那个格子。空间义转向社会意义：座位被人占住了。

senses.title: Occupy the mind: keep attention busy
senses.titleCN: 占据心思：让注意力忙个不停
senses.definition: to fill someone's thoughts or attention, especially for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 填满某人的思绪或注意力，尤指持续很久
senses.example: The question occupied him for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题盘踞在他心里好几周。
senses.why: Attention is another space. When a thought grips it, no other thought can get in, so occupy comes to mean 'absorb the mind'.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是另一种空间。当一个念头抓住它，别的念头就进不来，于是 occupy 表示“占据心思”。

senses.title: Military occupation: control without annexing
senses.titleCN: 军事占领：控制而不并入
senses.definition: to control a country or territory with armed force, usually without making it part of one's own state
senses.definitionCN: 以武力控制某国或某地区，通常不把它并入本国
senses.example: The army occupied the region for six years.
senses.exampleCN: 军队占领该地区六年。
senses.why: The oldest 'seize' sense scaled up to whole territories. Holding the ground is the point, and the legal status of the land is left open.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的“夺取”义放大到整片领土。要点在于握住土地，而土地的法律归属则悬置不论。

senses.title: Take a place in a ranking or order
senses.titleCN: 位居某一序列
senses.definition: to have or fill a particular place in a list, ranking or sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在名单、排名或序列中占有某个位置
senses.example: The novel occupies third place on the bestseller list.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说在畅销榜上位居第三。
senses.why: A rank is a numbered slot. The thing that holds that slot occupies it, even though nothing physical is gripped.
senses.whyCN: 名次是一个带编号的格子。占住该格子的东西就 occupy 它，尽管并没有任何实体被抓住。

senses.title: Occupy oneself: keep oneself busy
senses.titleCN: 使自己忙碌：给自己找事做
senses.definition: in the reflexive form occupy oneself with, to keep oneself busy with an activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于反身形式 occupy oneself with，表示让自己忙于某项活动
senses.example: He occupied himself with repairing the old clock.
senses.exampleCN: 他让自己忙着修那口旧钟。
senses.why: The reflexive turns the grip inward: instead of an outside thing holding you, you give your own time to an activity.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把“握”转向自身：不是外物抓住你，而是你把自己的时间交给一项活动。

senses.title: Archaic euphemism: have sex with
senses.titleCN: 古委婉语：与……发生性关系
senses.definition: in 16th and 17th century usage, a polite cover for having sexual intercourse with someone
senses.definitionCN: 在 16、17 世纪用法中，作为“与某人发生性关系”的委婉说法
senses.example: Renaissance writers used occupy as a discreet cover for a sexual act.
senses.exampleCN: 文艺复兴时期的作家用 occupy 隐晦地指代性行为。
senses.why: The 'take possession of a person' sense was pushed into sexual meaning in the early 15th century. Because of that, polite usage dropped the word for a time, and occupant could even mean a prostitute.
senses.whyCN: “占有一个人的身体”这一层在 15 世纪早期被推成性含义。正因如此，讲究礼貌的用法一度回避这个词，occupant 甚至可指妓女。

intro.en: Occupy arrived in English in the mid-14th century through Old French, from Latin occupare 'seize, take possession'. The ending is hard to explain, but the record is old; a 16th-17th century sexual euphemism later pushed the word out of polite use for a while.
intro.cn: occupy 于 14 世纪中期经古法语进入英语，来自拉丁语 occupare“夺取、占有”。词尾音节难以解释，但记录已很古老；16 至 17 世纪的性委婉义后来又使这个词一度退出礼貌用法。

items.en: Occupien is recorded meaning 'to take possession of and retain or keep'; the same period shows the senses 'fill space or time' and 'employ a person'.
items.cn: occupien 记录为“取得并保有、占住”；同一时期还出现“占据空间或时间”和“雇用某人”的义项。

items.en: Borrowed irregularly from Old French ocuper / occuper (13c.), or taken directly from Latin occupare.
items.cn: 不规则地借自古法语 ocuper / occuper（13 世纪），或直接取自拉丁语 occupare。

items.en: Latin occupare 'take over, seize, take into possession' is an emphatic form of ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp, seize'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 occupare“接管、夺取、占为己有”是 ob“覆于其上”加 capere“抓、夺”的强调形式。

items.en: Capere goes back to PIE *kap- 'to grasp', the root behind captive and capture as well.
items.cn: capere 追溯到原始印欧语 *kap-“抓”，captive 与 capture 也出自这个词根。

items.en: The sense 'have sexual intercourse with' is found from the early 15th century and served as a euphemism in the 16th and 17th centuries; Shakespeare uses it in Henry IV, Part 2, and occupant could then mean a prostitute.
items.cn: “与……发生性关系”义自 15 世纪早期可见，16、17 世纪成为委婉语；莎士比亚在《亨利四世下篇》用过它，当时的 occupant 还可指妓女。

items.en: Modern English keeps the neutral senses of holding space, time, office and attention, and forms occupation, occupant and occupancy from the same stem.
items.cn: 现代英语保留占据空间、时间、职位与注意力等中性义，并由同一词干构成 occupation、occupant、occupancy。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to happen or come to mind. It shares the ob- beginning but comes from currere 'to run', not from capere 'to seize'.
entries.definitionCN: 发生；想到。它同样以 ob- 开头，但词根是 currere“跑”，不是 capere“抓”。

entries.definition: a person who lives in or uses a place. It is the noun built on occupy, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 居住者；占用者。它是 occupy 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: absorbed in one's own thoughts. The pre- 'before' adds the idea of the mind being taken up in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 心事重重的；出神的。pre-“预先”加了“心思先被占去”的意思。

entries.definition: to take hold of something suddenly and by force. It stresses the grab, while occupy stresses keeping possession.
entries.definitionCN: 突然用力抓住。它强调抓的动作，occupy 强调占住不放。

entries.definition: to live in a place as its population. It is used of people and animals, while occupy can also mean simply filling space.
entries.definitionCN: 作为居民住在某地。它多用于人和动物，occupy 也可仅指占据空间。

entries.definition: to attract and hold someone's interest. It focuses on the attraction, while occupy focuses on the attention being filled up.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引并保持某人的兴趣。它侧重吸引力，occupy 侧重注意力被填满。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin ob plus capere, the capere family in capture and captive, and the modern nouns occupation and occupant.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + capere，capture 与 captive 中的 capere 词族，以及现代名词 occupation 与 occupant。

normal.en: ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp' gives 'grasp over something': the hand closes on it and holds.
normal.cn: ob“覆于其上”加 capere“抓”就是“在上面抓住”：手合拢握住不放。

normal.en: Capture and captive share the same capere root, so all three words are about a grip that does not let go.
normal.cn: capture 与 captive 同出 capere，因此这三个词都围绕“握住不放”。

normal.en: Obtain uses tenere 'to hold', occur uses currere 'to run': same ob- prefix, three different roots.
normal.cn: obtain 用 tenere“握持”，occur 用 currere“跑”：同一个 ob- 前缀，三个不同词根。

normal.en: Occupation is both a job and a military takeover, because both are a held place.
normal.cn: occupation 既是职业也是军事占领，因为两者都是“占住的位置”。

normal.en: Occupy oneself with is the reflexive branch: you give your own time to a task.
normal.cn: occupy oneself with 是反身分支：你把自己的时间交给一项任务。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed flat on a table: the table under it is no longer free, and that is occupy in one gesture.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌平压在桌面上：掌下的桌面不再空着，这就是 occupy 的一个动作。

abstract.en: The same hand can close on a building, an afternoon, a chair, a rank, or a thought.
abstract.cn: 同一只手可以握住一栋楼、一个下午、一把椅子、一个名次或一个念头。

abstract.en: When the grip turns inward, the hand holds its own time: that is occupy oneself.
abstract.cn: 当这只手握向自身，它握的是自己的时间：这就是 occupy oneself。

examples.en: A single bookshelf occupied the entire wall of the small study.
examples.cn: 一个书架占满了小书房整面墙。

examples.en: Rebuilding the harbour occupied the town for three summers.
examples.cn: 重建港口让全镇忙了三个夏天。

examples.en: The reporter was occupied with verifying the source and missed the call.
examples.cn: 记者正忙着核实消息来源，错过了那通电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥 Q 派」——奥 Q 派的人一进门就占了整间会议室 → occupy 占据、占用

root: 源自拉丁语 occupare“夺取、占有”= ob-“覆于其上、对着”+ capere“抓、夺”（PIE *kap-“抓”），核心是“抓住并占住不放”；词尾音节来源难以解释。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of occupy all start from one gesture: a hand closes over something and holds it. The same grip then measures floors, hours, homes, posts, ranks, attention and, in the oldest branch, whole territories.
sensesIntro.cn: occupy 的十个义项都从同一个动作出发：手合拢抓住某物并握住。同一只握持之手随后量出地板、小时、住所、职位、名次、注意力，以及最古老分支里的整片领土。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing over something and holding it tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢抓住某物，紧紧握住不放。

branches.en: SEIZURE: taking a thing or a whole territory by force and keeping control of it.
branches.cn: 夺取：以武力拿下一件东西或整片领土，并保持控制。

branches.en: SPACE, TIME AND HOME: the grip becomes the floor a thing covers, the hours an activity uses, and the house a family lives in.
branches.cn: 空间、时间与住所：握持变成物体覆盖的地面、活动用掉的时间，以及一家人居住的房子。

branches.en: POSITION: a post or a rank is a slot in an institution or a list, and its holder fills that slot.
branches.cn: 位置：职位或名次是机构或名单中的格子，担任者把它填满。

branches.en: BUSY MIND: attention can be gripped from outside, or handed over by oneself in the reflexive form.
branches.cn: 忙碌的心神：注意力既可以被外物抓住，也可以在反身形式里由自己交出。

branches.en: THE OLD EUPHEMISM: possessing a person was pushed into sexual meaning, a branch polite usage later abandoned.
branches.cn: 旧委婉语：“占有人”被推成性含义，这一分支后来被礼貌用法弃用。

intro.en: Occupy is Latin ob- 'over, against' plus capere 'to grasp', with the verb ending -are. English keeps the stem occup- and builds nouns with -ation, -ant, -ancy and -ier.
intro.cn: occupy 由拉丁语 ob-“覆于其上、对着”加 capere“抓”和动词词尾 -are 构成。英语保留词干 occup-，并用 -ation、-ant、-ancy、-ier 造名词。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin occupare, an emphatic compound of ob and capere; capere 'to grasp' is the root at the centre.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 occupare，即 ob 与 capere 的强调复合词；中心的词根是 capere“抓”。

items.meaning: to seize and hold; to fill space, time or attention
items.meaningCN: 占据；占用；占领；使忙碌
items.example: Two guards occupy the gate at all times.
items.exampleCN: 两名卫兵始终守着大门。

items.meaning: a person who lives in or uses a place
items.meaningCN: 居住者；占用者；乘坐者（-ant 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The new occupant moved in last Friday.
items.exampleCN: 新住户上周五搬了进来。

items.meaning: the state of being occupied; the rate of use
items.meaningCN: 占用；居住；入住率（-ancy 构成状态名词）
items.example: Hotel occupancy falls sharply in winter.
items.exampleCN: 旅馆入住率在冬季大幅下降。

items.meaning: a job; the act of taking control of a place
items.meaningCN: 职业；占领；占用（-ation 构成行为或状态名词）
items.example: She lists her occupation as 'translator'.
items.exampleCN: 她把自己的职业填作“译者”。

items.meaning: relating to a job or the workplace
items.meaningCN: 职业的；职业引起的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Noise is a common occupational hazard in factories.
items.exampleCN: 噪音是工厂里常见的职业危害。

items.meaning: the person who occupies a property or territory
items.meaningCN: 占据者；占领者；住户
items.example: The occupier of the flat is responsible for repairs.
items.exampleCN: 该公寓的住户负责维修。

items.meaning: absorbed in one's own thoughts; already taken up
items.meaningCN: 心事重重的；专注的（pre-“预先”+ occupy，心思先被占去）
items.example: He was too preoccupied to notice the rain.
items.exampleCN: 他心事太重，没注意到下雨。

items.meaning: a thought or subject that fills the mind
items.meaningCN: 全神贯注的事；心头大事
items.example: Safety became his main preoccupation.
items.exampleCN: 安全成了他心头最挂念的事。

items.structure: capt- (grasp, from capere) + -ure (noun and verb ending)
items.meaning: to take by force or to record an image
items.meaningCN: 俘获；夺取；捕捉（影像）
items.example: The camera captured the whole scene.
items.exampleCN: 相机拍下了整个场景。

items.meaning: kept in confinement; a prisoner
items.meaningCN: 被关押的；俘虏（同一“抓”词根）
items.example: The captive birds were released at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 被关的鸟在黎明时被放走了。

latinEntries.meaning: to take over, seize, take into possession

definition_zh: 发生；出现；存在；被想到；在文中出现
definition_en: to happen, to present itself, to be found somewhere, or to come into the mind
core_image: 两样东西在同一条路上迎面跑来，一头撞上
scene: A fault occurred in the cooling system during the night shift.
sceneCN: 这里 occur 是「发生、出现」（第 2 个义项：事件发生）；句意：夜班期间冷却系统出现了故障。图中可辨识物件：亮起的警报灯、冷却管道、值班人员、夜班记录本。

pos.zh: 发生；出现；存在；（想法）浮现
